action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

page_token.description: list only: the `next_page_token` a listing of the same scope gave, to list the artifacts after it.

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (writing people will keep editing or pass around as text, such as a memo, plan, spec, proposal or notes), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a page to look at or use: an explainer, a diagram, anything interactive, a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Base directory for this skill: /home/kato/Projects/blender-models/.claude/skills/archviz-film-upgrade # VDC-to-archviz film upgrade ## How this fits this repo (read first; overrides the directive where they differ) - **Scope:** presentation films only (e.g. `highland/walkthrough`, `deliverables/archviz`). Review renders keep their provenance colors and plan/iso cameras. Coordination and work-sequence films (e.g. the `highland/risers` Corridor 108 sequence) keep their own framing and may end in a corridor; Rule 3 doesn't apply to them. - **Realism never changes geometry** (`docs/METHOD.md`). The bevel is a shader effect, which is fine. The section rig in Module B adds non-destructive modifiers to a presentation scene only, never to a spec build. Every film still carries the "illustrative, not a contract document" strip. - **Diagnostic frames (section 0):** write them under `build///diagnostics/` (git-ignored), not `/tmp`; scripts take the path from `$BM_BUILD` or an argument, never a hard-coded one. Look at every frame with the Read tool and say in the report which frames you looked at. "Ran without errors" doesn't count as checked (the repo's "checks passed" and "looked at the renders" rule). On CPU, a 1920×1080 frame at 32 samples can take minutes on a heavy scene, so render the diagnostics at 25% while iterating and save 50% for the final pass. - **Where it runs:** `scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'` only on RunPod (`products/*/runpod_*.sh`). This laptop and CI render on CPU; for CPU previews set the device to `'CPU'` and lower the resolution and samples. - **`device = 'GPU'` alone is not enough headless.** Script 2 never enables a compute device, so Cycles quietly renders on CPU. Use `configure_device()` in `projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema.py`: it sets `compute_device_type` (`OPTIX`/`CUDA`), enables the devices and exits if none is found, so it never falls back silently. - **House example:** `projects/highland/products/walkthrough/` (`CINEMA.md`, `cinema.shots.json`, `cinema.py`, `cinema_score.py`, `cinema_finish.py`) already implements most of section 8: a shot list as data, cuts on musical beats, level lens-shifted cameras, motion blur, frame claiming across parallel GPU workers, benchmarking, a graded finish and an original score. Extend it or copy its patterns before writing a new pipeline. - **Section 8** (the end of this file) holds the repo's own agency-grade additions to the directive. Apply them together with it. - **Existing compositor:** Script 2 deletes the scene's current `compositing_node_group`. Look at what it does first (e.g. a caption or disclaimer pass) and rebuild that into the new tree. - **Boolean solver:** use `'MANIFOLD'`, not `'EXACT'`. Exact fails on the coplanar faces architectural meshes always have. - **Lens distortion bends straight lines,** which works against Rule 1. Keep `Distortion` at 0 and use dispersion only if wanted. - **Tested 2026-11-06 on headless bpy 5.0.1:** all three scripts run on a test scene. The compositor renders (not black), camera keys come out `LINEAR`, the marker binds the camera, and the guardrail table's node names and socket names match this build. One fix was made: Module C sets `portal_data.cycles.is_portal` (plain `is_portal` raises `AttributeError` in 5.0.1). - **Code placement:** if these scripts get reused, port them into `src/bmodels/` as shared code (repo root from `bmodels.paths.ROOT`, no hard-coded paths) instead of copying them into each product. Committed `.blend` files stay self-contained (packed assets). --- # Agent Directive: Universal $20k VDC-to-Archviz Upgrade Pipeline (Blender 5.0+) ## 0. PRIME DIRECTIVE: The Visual Verification Loop (Never Fly Blind) You are a visual artist, not just a code generator. A Python script that executes without errors DOES NOT mean the shot looks good. BIM/VDC geometry frequently contains offset origins, flipped normals, overlapping coplanar faces (Z-fighting), and unapplied scales that break procedural assumptions. For EVERY camera shot and lighting setup you create, you MUST execute this closed-loop verification cycle before moving on: 1. **Render a Fast Diagnostic Frame:** Programmatically render the start, middle, and end frames of each shot at 50% resolution (`1920x1080`, `32` Cycles samples with OIDN enabled) to a temporary directory (`/tmp/vdc_audit_frame_XXXX.png`). 2. **Visually Inspect the Output (Multimodal Vision + Histogram Check):** Load and inspect the rendered PNG image. Audit it against five strict visual criteria: - **Obstruction Check:** Is the camera clipped inside a wall, mullion, door, or ceiling? - **Composition & Balance:** Are vertical lines parallel to the frame edges? Does the floor or ceiling occupy more than 45% of the frame (adjust `shift_y` if so)? - **Lighting Ratio (Contrast):** Is the image flat and evenly lit? Every luxury shot requires a clear hierarchy of light: a bright focal destination, mid-tone architectural surfaces, and soft contact shadows grounding the floor/wall intersections. - **Highlight/Shadow Clipping:** Are emissive fixtures blooming naturally, or are walls blown out to pure `#FFFFFF` white or crushed into noisy `#000000` black? - **Scale & Tactility:** Do materials read at the right real-world UV scale (e.g., brick courses, wood planks, carpet tiles), or are textures stretched/microscopic because object scale wasn't applied (`bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)`)? 3. **Iterate Until It Passes:** If a diagnostic frame fails ANY of the five checks above, adjust the camera coordinates, light power/angles, or UV mapping and re-render the diagnostic frame until the image looks like an architectural photograph. ## 1. Mission & Role You are a Lead Technical Artist and Blender 5.0+ Python (`bpy`) Automation Agent. Your objective is to transform raw Virtual Design & Construction (VDC), BIM, or CAD geometry imports inside **Blender 5.x** into **ultra-high-end, path-traced architectural films**. Raw VDC exports look like engineering diagrams because they suffer from six systemic flaws: 1. Clipped highlight values and narrow-gamut color management. 2. Unnatural continuous "robot spline" camera paths that clip through doors and stare into corners. 3. Razor-sharp 90-degree polygon edges and flat, zero-imperfection shaders. 4. Blown-out emissive ceiling strips and visible light-source specular blobs. 5. Technical cross-sections that reveal untextured background massing. 6. Lack of narrative emotional payoff ("Compression & Release"). --- ## 2. CRITICAL: Blender 5.0+ Breaking API Guardrails (Do Not Use 4.x Syntax) Blender 5.0+ removed legacy shortcuts that dominate older training data. Enforce these exact **Blender 5.x API patterns**: | System | Deprecated (Blender 4.x — FAILS in 5.x) | Required Blender 5.0+ Syntax | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Compositor Tree** | `scene.use_nodes = True`
`scene.node_tree` (`AttributeError`) | `tree = bpy.data.node_groups.new("Archviz_Comp", "CompositorNodeTree")`
`scene.compositing_node_group = tree` | | **Compositor Output** | `nodes.new('CompositorNodeComposite')` (Removed) | `tree.interface.new_socket(name="Image", in_out="OUTPUT", socket_type="NodeSocketColor")`
`out = tree.nodes.new("NodeGroupOutput")` | | **Compositor Node Options** | `glare.glare_type = 'FOG_GLOW'`
`glare.size = 7`
`lens.use_fit = True` | Node options are now **Input Sockets** using UI-label strings & `0.0–1.0` floats:
`glare.inputs["Type"].default_value = "Fog Glow"`
`glare.inputs["Quality"].default_value = "High"`
`glare.inputs["Size"].default_value = 0.65`
`lens.inputs["Distortion"].default_value = -0.008`
`lens.inputs["Dispersion"].default_value = 0.0035`
`lens.inputs["Fit"].default_value = True` | | **Removed Comp Nodes** | `CompositorNodeMixRGB`, `CompositorNodeGamma`, `CompositorNodeMapRange` | Use unified Shader nodes inside the Compositor:
`ShaderNodeMix`, `ShaderNodeGamma`, `ShaderNodeMapRange` | | **Animation F-Curves** | `action.fcurves` (`AttributeError` — Slotted Actions required) | Use `bpy_extras.anim_utils`:
`cb = anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(action, obj.animation_data.action_slot)`
`for fcurve in cb.fcurves:` | | **Property Access** | `scene['cycles']` (Dict-style access removed for `bpy.props`) | Always use dot-attribute syntax: `scene.cycles.samples` | | **Material / World Nodes** | `mat.use_nodes = True` (Deprecated no-op in 5.x) | Always on by default in 5.0+, or guarded gracefully. | --- ## 3. Universal Architectural & Cinematography Rules ### Rule 1: Two-Point Perspective (Architectural Tilt-Shift) * **Never tilt an architectural camera up or down.** Vertical architectural lines (walls, columns, doorframes, mullions) must remain 100% parallel to the frame edges. * Lock every camera's `rotation_euler.x = math.radians(90)` and `rotation_euler.y = 0.0`. * Frame vertical elevation exclusively via `camera.data.shift_y` (`-0.05` to `+0.15`). * Use `24mm–35mm` focal lengths (`36mm` full-frame sensor width) in **16:9 Widescreen** (`3840x2160`). ### Rule 2: Multi-Camera Linear Cuts Over Single-Spline Paths * Never use a single continuous camera spline that twists 90 degrees inside tight corridors or ghosts through closed doors. * Break the journey into discrete **3-to-5-second cinematic shots** (`CAM_01`, `CAM_02`, etc.) bound to Timeline Markers. * Force **100% `LINEAR` keyframe interpolation** on all camera location/rotation f-curves via the Blender 5.0+ Slotted Action `channelbag` so movement feels like a constant-velocity Steadicam across cuts. * Keyframe any door in the camera's path open (`75°–90°` swing or slide) prior to the camera crossing the threshold. ### Rule 3: Narrative "Compression & Release" * Never end an architectural tour in an enclosed service space (corridors, stairwells, mechanical rooms, or elevator lobbies). * Circulation spaces are the **Compression Phase** (controlled, warm 3500K artificial light). The final 20% of the timeline must transition into a **Release Phase**—a sunlit destination with high ceilings, natural exterior light (`2800K–4000K` low-angle sun + Sky Portals), and exterior context views. ### Rule 4: Separate Fixture Glow from Scene Illumination * Clamp visible light fixture `Emission` nodes to `Strength: 3.0–5.0` (`#FFF4E6` warm white) so the fixture reads as diffused acrylic under AgX / ACES 2.0 color management. * Place actual Blender `AREA` lights (`Spread: 85°–105°`) just below ceiling fixtures and inside coves to cast physical light falloff, and set `light_obj.visible_camera = False` and `light_obj.visible_glossy = False` so they never create artificial specular hotspots on doors, glass, or polished floors. --- ## 4. Script 1: `01_scene_audit_b5.py` (Blender 5.0+ Scene Inspector) Run this first to inspect collections, spatial bounds, slotted animations, and engine settings. ```python import bpy import mathutils def audit_vdc_scene_b5(): scene = bpy.context.scene print("\n================ BLENDER 5.0+ VDC SCENE AUDIT ================") print(f"Blender Version: {bpy.app.version_string}") print(f"File: {bpy.data.filepath or 'Unsaved File'}") print(f"Engine: {scene.render.engine} | FPS: {scene.render.fps} | Frames: {scene.frame_start}-{scene.frame_end}") print("\n1. COLLECTIONS:") for col in bpy.data.collections: print(f" - {col.name}: {len(col.objects)} objects") meshes = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'MESH' and not o.hide_render] if meshes: min_co = mathutils.Vector((1e9, 1e9, 1e9)) max_co = mathutils.Vector((-1e9, -1e9, -1e9)) for obj in meshes: for corner in obj.bound_box: world_co = obj.matrix_world @ mathutils.Vector(corner) min_co.x = min(min_co.x, world_co.x) min_co.y = min(min_co.y, world_co.y) min_co.z = min(min_co.z, world_co.z) max_co.x = max(max_co.x, world_co.x) max_co.y = max(max_co.y, world_co.y) max_co.z = max(max_co.z, world_co.z) print(f"\n2. WORLD BOUNDS (Meters):") print(f" - Min (X,Y,Z): ({min_co.x:.2f}, {min_co.y:.2f}, {min_co.z:.2f})") print(f" - Max (X,Y,Z): ({max_co.x:.2f}, {max_co.y:.2f}, {max_co.z:.2f})") print(f" - Footprint: {(max_co.x - min_co.x):.2f}m x {(max_co.y - min_co.y):.2f}m x {(max_co.z - min_co.z):.2f}m tall") print("\n3. Script 3: `03_cinematic_rigs_b5.py` (Blender 5.0 Slotted Action Cameras, X-Ray Section & Portals) Import or invoke these reusable functions to build multi-camera cuts using **Blender 5.0+ Slotted Actions (`channelbag`)**, glowing Boolean architectural cross-sections, and Golden-Hour "Release" lighting rigs. ```python import bpy from bpy_extras import anim_utils import math # ============================================================================= # HELPER: ENFORCE LINEAR INTERPOLATION IN BLENDER 5.0+ SLOTTED ACTIONS # ============================================================================= def set_linear_interpolation_b5(obj): """ Reaches into the Blender 5.0+ Slotted Action channelbag for the given object and forces all keyframe points to LINEAR interpolation. """ anim = obj.animation_data if not anim or not anim.action or not anim.action_slot: return channelbag = anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(anim.action, anim.action_slot) if channelbag: for fcurve in channelbag.fcurves: for kf in fcurve.keyframe_points: kf.interpolation = 'LINEAR' # ============================================================================= # MODULE A: CREATE ARCHITECTURAL TILT-SHIFT CAMERA SHOT (BLENDER 5.0+) # ============================================================================= def create_archviz_shot_b5(name, frame_start, frame_end, start_loc, end_loc, yaw_deg, lens_mm=28.0, shift_y=0.0, dof_dist=0.0): """ Creates a level 2-point perspective camera with LINEAR Steadicam motion using Blender 5.0 Slotted Action channelbags and binds it to a timeline marker. """ scene = bpy.context.scene cam_col = bpy.data.collections.get("Archviz_Cameras") if not cam_col: cam_col = bpy.data.collections.new("Archviz_Cameras") scene.collection.children.link(cam_col) cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new(name) cam_data.lens = lens_mm cam_data.sensor_width = 36.0 cam_data.shift_y = shift_y cam_data.passepartout_alpha = 0.95 cam_data.show_composition_thirds = True cam_data.show_composition_center = True if dof_dist > 0.0: cam_data.dof.use_dof = True cam_data.dof.focus_distance = dof_dist cam_data.dof.aperture_fstop = 4.0 cam_obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cam_data) cam_col.objects.link(cam_obj) # Lock X=90°, Y=0° so vertical lines never converge cam_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(yaw_deg)) cam_obj.location = start_loc cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_start) cam_obj.location = end_loc cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_end) # Set linear interpolation via Blender 5.0 channelbag API set_linear_interpolation_b5(cam_obj) marker = scene.timeline_markers.new(name=name, frame=frame_start) marker.camera = cam_obj return cam_obj # ============================================================================= # MODULE B: ANIMATED BOOLEAN X-RAY SECTION RIG (BLENDER 5.0+) # ============================================================================= def create_boolean_section_rig_b5(target_objects, location, dimensions, frame_in, frame_hold_start, frame_hold_end, frame_out): """ Creates an invisible animated Boolean cutter box that slices open a list of target architectural meshes and applies a glowing gold emissive shader ONLY to the sliced cross-section faces. """ cut_mat = bpy.data.materials.get("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow") or bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow") nodes = cut_mat.node_tree.nodes nodes.clear() emiss = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission') emiss.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.78, 0.45, 1.0) # Architectural gold emiss.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 6.0 out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial') cut_mat.node_tree.links.new(emiss.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface']) bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=location) cutter = bpy.context.active_object cutter.name = "VDC_Boolean_Section_Cutter" cutter.display_type = 'WIRE' cutter.visible_camera = False cutter.visible_diffuse = False cutter.visible_glossy = False cutter.visible_shadow = False cutter.data.materials.append(cut_mat) cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001) cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_in) cutter.scale = dimensions cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_start) cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_end) cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001) cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_out) set_linear_interpolation_b5(cutter) for obj in target_objects: if obj.type == 'MESH' and obj != cutter: if cut_mat.name not in obj.data.materials: obj.data.materials.append(cut_mat) mod = obj.modifiers.new(name="VDC_Section_Cut", type='BOOLEAN') mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE' mod.object = cutter mod.solver = 'EXACT' return cutter # ============================================================================= # MODULE C: NATURAL LIGHT "RELEASE" PORTAL & SUN RIG # ============================================================================= def create_golden_hour_window_rig_b5(window_location, window_yaw_deg, width=6.0, height=3.0, sun_elevation_deg=10.0): """ Places a Cycles Sky Portal directly over an exterior window opening alongside a low-angle 2800K Golden Hour Sun to create dramatic interior light shafts. """ scene = bpy.context.scene # 1. Cycles Interior Sky Portal portal_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Window_Portal", type='AREA') portal_data.shape = 'RECTANGLE' portal_data.size = width portal_data.size_y = height portal_data.cycles.is_portal = True # Blender 5.x: the portal flag is a Cycles light property portal_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Window_Portal", portal_data) scene.collection.objects.link(portal_obj) portal_obj.location = window_location portal_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg)) # 2. Warm 2800K Directional Sunset Light sun_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Golden_Sun", type='SUN') sun_data.energy = 4.5 sun_data.color = (1.0, 0.74, 0.48) sun_data.angle = math.radians(2.5) sun_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Golden_Sun", sun_data) scene.collection.objects.link(sun_obj) sun_obj.location = window_location sun_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90.0 - sun_elevation_deg), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg + 15.0)) return portal_obj, sun_obj ``` --- ## 7. Pre-Render Verification Checklist (Blender 5.0+) Before rendering final frames or animations, the agent must verify: - [ ] **Blender 5.0 Compositor Verified:** `scene.compositing_node_group` is assigned and terminates in a linked `NodeGroupOutput` node with a `NodeSocketColor` output interface socket (unlinked output produces black frames). - [ ] **Slotted Action Linear Motion:** All animated cameras have had their f-curves set to `LINEAR` via `anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot()`. - [ ] **No Vertical Convergence:** Every active camera has `rotation_euler.x == 90°` and `rotation_euler.y == 0°`. - [ ] **No Geometry Clipping:** No camera passes through closed doors, mullions, or walls at any frame. - [ ] **No Light Specular Blobs:** All filler `AREA` and `POINT` lights have `visible_camera = False` and `visible_glossy = False`. - [ ] **Emotional Payoff Delivered:** The final 20% of the timeline transitions out of artificial interior circulation into a naturally lit destination space. --- ## 8. Agency-grade additions (repo maintainers, 2026-11-06) What separates a $100k agency film from a good render is mostly decided before Cycles runs: the brief, the boards, the edit and the sound. Then comes discipline about light and material values, and a QC pass nobody skips. Every API named below was checked against bpy 5.0.1 on 2026-11-06. ### 8.1 Pre-production (decide the film before building it) - **Brief in one sentence:** who watches it (owner, board, residents, jury), what they must believe at the end, and the runtime. 45–90 s is the usual length for an owner or marketing film; residents need 20–40 s per notice. - **Reference board:** 6–10 frames from real architectural photography and agency films, one per shot, noting lens, camera height, time of day and light direction. Match a mood, never copy a frame. - **Shot list as data:** one JSON entry per shot with lens, shift, keys, focus and an exposure trim, like `cinema.shots.json`. Code reads it, so changing the edit doesn't mean editing code. - **Animatic first:** 10–25% resolution, 4–8 samples, Cycles. Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames headless, so Cycles is the only option here. Cut it to the music before spending any real render time. Agencies lock the edit at animatic stage; re-cutting after final renders is the most expensive mistake. - **Cut to music:** shot lengths in whole beats (e.g. 80 BPM: 3 s = 4 beats), with chord changes on the cuts. `cinema_score.py` shows how. - **Handles:** render 8–12 extra frames at both ends of every shot so the edit can slip without re-rendering. ### 8.2 VDC/BIM import hygiene (fix the model before lighting it) - **Recenter near the origin.** BIM exports often sit at state-plane or survey coordinates, hundreds of km from 0. Float precision then makes animated cameras jitter and causes shadow and z-fighting artifacts. Move the model so the area of interest is within about 1 km of the origin, and record the offset as a custom property so it can be undone. - **Apply scale and rotation** (`transform_apply(location=False, rotation=True, scale=True)`), recalculate normals, and merge by distance at 0.1 mm. - **Find and fix coplanar duplicates.** Hunt for z-fighting with a diagnostic frame at grazing angles: overlapping slabs and finishes, a wall drawn twice by two trades. Delete the duplicate or offset it by 1 mm, and record which one stays (the governing trade). - **Keep identity.** Carry the IFC GlobalId or Revit element ID into `cie_id` and other custom properties, so a frame can be traced back to the element that drew it. Import IFC with `ifcopenshell` (not installed; `uv add ifcopenshell` and check `uv lock` keeps numpy<2 for bpy) or the Bonsai extension. Speckle is an option for live Revit to Blender. - **Bevel what the camera sees.** The Bevel shader in the directive is costly per sample and doesn't change silhouettes. For hero objects in close-up shots, a Bevel modifier (2–3 mm, `harden_normals`) plus a WeightedNormal modifier looks better and renders faster. Use it only in the presentation scene, never in a spec build. ### 8.3 Cameras and motion - **Heights:** interiors at 1.2–1.5 m (just below eye level reads as more generous). Exteriors at 1.6 m for pedestrian views, or 4–15 m for a modest elevated view. Drone-height views are for context only. - **Speeds:** a dolly or slider moves at 0.2–0.6 m/s. Any faster reads as a video game. Pans are rare and slow (under 5°/s). - **Detail inserts:** 50–85 mm, still level (Rule 1), shallow depth of field (f/2–f/4) on materials and hardware. One insert every 3–4 shots gives the edit rhythm. The house film's walnut slat insert is an example. Wider shots stay at f/5.6–f/11 so the architecture stays sharp. - **Bokeh:** set `dof.aperture_blades` to 7–9 and a small `aperture_rotation`; round bokeh from blades = 0 reads as CG. - **Motion blur on:** `render.use_motion_blur = True`, `motion_blur_shutter = 0.5` (180°). Without it, linear camera moves strobe. - **Handheld life (optional):** an `FModifierNoise` on the location f-curves only (0.5–2 mm amplitude, slow). Never put it on rotation, because Rule 1 locks the camera level. - **Unwrap yaw when keying cameras from `atan2`** (found on the Highland film, 2026-11-08). A camera looking along −x sits on the ±π seam, so a few mm of drift flips the key from +90° to −270°. That's the same direction, but Blender interpolates Euler keys, so inside the motion-blur shutter the camera spins 360°. The result is two washed-out, ghosted frames that a quaternion-based "rotation step" check reports as 0°. Keep yaw continuous (`yaw += 2π·round((prev−yaw)/2π)`), and validate the Euler key steps themselves, not only the quaternion difference. Wider lesson: run the automated flicker check (8.8) on the finished film; the 3-frames-per-shot diagnostics missed this. - **Exterior camera distance is limited by the site.** At 2.39:1 a 24 mm lens frames less height than at 16:9. On a narrow street you can't back up across it (the Highland camera ended up inside the OSM massing opposite, which validation caught), so gain distance along the street with an oblique view instead. - **Aspect ratio:** 16:9 per the directive. For marketing films, 2.39:1 is a valid option (the house film uses it); render 16:9 and crop, or set the resolution directly. ### 8.4 Light (get the values physical, then make it beautiful) - **Sky:** `ShaderNodeTexSky` with `sky_type = 'MULTIPLE_SCATTERING'` for physically based daylight. Or an HDRI from Poly Haven (`bmodels.polyhaven`, checksum-locked, CC0) when real cloud and context reflections matter. Rotate the sun to the site's true north and a real date and time, and record both. - **Color temperature:** set `light.use_temperature = True` and `light.temperature` in kelvin. That avoids hand-picked RGB: 2700–3000 K for residential, 3500 K for corridors (the directive's compression phase), 4000 K for back-of-house. Use `ShaderNodeBlackbody` for emissive fixtures, so a fixture's glow matches its light. - **Real fixtures:** when the fixture schedule names a product, drive the area or spot light with that manufacturer's IES file (`ShaderNodeTexIES`). Wall-washer scallops are what make a corridor look real. - **Exposure, not wattage:** balance a shot with `view_settings.exposure` (per shot, from the shot list's exposure trim) and `light.exposure`. Don't scale every light up. - **Light linking:** `obj.light_linking.receiver_collection` / `blocker_collection` (Cycles) for a rim on one object or a kicker on the hero material without spilling everywhere. Use it sparingly and only in presentation scenes. - **Light groups:** add `view_layer.lightgroups` (e.g. `sun`, `sky`, `interior`, `fixtures`) and set `obj.lightgroup`. The balance between day and fixtures can then be re-graded in post without re-rendering. It's the cheapest agency trick there is. - **Noise control:** `cycles.use_light_tree` (on by default) for many fixtures. `cycles.use_guiding = True` (path guiding, CPU only) helps interiors lit through windows. `blur_glossy` at 0.5–1.0, caustics off (`caustics_reflective`/`caustics_refractive = False`) unless they're the subject. - **Color views:** AgX "AgX - Medium High Contrast" is the default and verified. "AgX - Punchy" works for exterior dusk. "ACES 2.0" and "Khronos PBR Neutral" also exist in this build. Pick one per film and never mix them. Note that in 5.0.1 the look names carry the "AgX - " prefix. ### 8.5 Materials, scale and dressing - **Albedo discipline:** the brightest real paint is about 0.8–0.85 linear albedo, so never use 1.0 white. Black materials stay at 0.02–0.04 or above. Concrete sits around 0.3–0.4 and wood around 0.2–0.45. Most "CG look" comes from albedos that are too bright or too saturated. - **Real-world mapping:** for BIM without UVs, use box projection (`ShaderNodeTexImage.projection = 'BOX'`, `projection_blend` 0.1–0.2) in object or world space, in metres. `bmodels.polyhaven` already does this. Diagnostic check: a brick course is 75 mm with a 10 mm joint (UK/metric) or 2⅝" per course (US modular), and carpet tiles are 500–610 mm. - **Break repetition:** use `ShaderNodeObjectInfo` → Random to vary hue, value and roughness by ±2–5% per object (doors, tiles, planks). Rotate and offset texture coordinates per object too. - **Wear where it would really occur:** use `ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion` or Pointiness (Cycles) for faint grime in corners and wear on edges. Keep it under 5% in a new building. "New construction" should look new, not dirty. - **Glass:** model glazing with real thickness, IOR 1.5 and a faint green-blue tint. Use portals at window openings (the directive's Module C) instead of hiding glass from shadow rays, which leaks light. - **People and life:** a few scaled, animated 3D people (licensed, e.g. Renderpeople or AXYZ anima), sitting or walking slowly, motion-blurred. Never more than the space would really hold. In occupied-building films, people must not suggest residents in unsafe positions near work zones. - **Vegetation:** scatter with Geometry Nodes using Poly Haven or licensed plant assets, with density and scale variation (±15%), and wind as a slow noise on a GN rotation. See the `scenario-blender-geometry-nodes` skill. - **Licensing:** record every downloaded asset's source, license and checksum (`bmodels.polyhaven` writes the lock for Poly Haven). Prefer CC0 (Poly Haven, ambientCG). Megascans/Fab and paid people libraries have per-project terms, so check them before they appear in a client deliverable. ### 8.6 Rendering pipeline - **Profiles:** at least three (animatic, preview, final), like `PROFILES` in `cinema.py`. Benchmark one frame per shot before launching a sequence, and estimate total hours. `cinema.py --bench` is the example. - **Final quality:** noise threshold 0.005–0.01 with enough max samples that the denoiser does little work. An over-denoised animation smears and flickers frame to frame. Keep `use_animated_seed = False` for stills; for animation, test both on a 2 s clip and look at the flicker. - **`render.use_persistent_data = True`** for sequences (it keeps the BVH and textures between frames). - **Render to EXR, grade later:** see 8.6a. Never bake a look into PNGs you can't re-grade. - **Parallel GPUs:** one frame per worker with a claim file, like `claim_frames`/`check_claim` in `cinema.py`. The same Blender (5.0.1) and the same `uv.lock` on every worker, with the source scene hash recorded per frame. - **Committed scenes stay self-contained:** pack textures, HDRIs and sounds before saving (`bm audit-blends`). ### 8.6a Studio EXR and AOV pipeline (tested on bpy 5.0.1, 2026-11-06) Why it matters: when a client asks for "the oak floor 15% lighter, the brick warmer", Cryptomatte plus light groups in a multilayer EXR sequence turn that into a compositor re-grade instead of a full Cycles re-render. Depth, mist and normals give depth haze and relighting tricks in post. What the tests on this repo's bpy 5.0.1 showed: | Claim | Result | |---|---| | `file_format = 'OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER'` | Fails on its own (`enum not found`). Set `image_settings.media_type = 'MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE'` first. | | Half float corrupts Cryptomatte and depth | No. With `color_depth = '16'`, Blender 5 writes Combined and albedo as half, and Depth, Vector, Cryptomatte and the denoising normal and depth as 32-bit float on its own. | | `DWAA` is safe for every pass | Not assumed. DWAA is lossy, and Blender applies it to every part of the file, Cryptomatte included. Use a lossless codec (`PIZ` or `ZIP`) whenever Cryptomatte, depth or vectors are in the file. Keep DWAA for beauty-only proxies. | | Temporal denoising | `bpy.ops.cycles.denoise_animation` exists, but in 5.0.1 it needs Denoising Data, the Vector pass and `use_exr_interleave = True` (it can't read the default multi-part layout). With OIDN on CPU it is **not** temporal: a frame's result didn't change when its neighbour changed. Whether it is temporal with OptiX on an NVIDIA GPU is untested. Until it's shown, fight flicker with samples (noise threshold ≤ 0.01) and a light denoise, and check flicker in QC (8.8). | | Vector pass with Cycles motion blur on | Cycles still writes a Vector pass. Its usefulness wasn't checked. Keep render-time motion blur for this repo's films: post vector blur smears transparency (x-ray sections, glass) and depth of field. | | Persistent data saves 25–40% | Measured on the Highland cinema scene (lobby, CPU, 640 × 268, 8 samples): frames 2–5 took 33.6 s with it vs 44.7 s without (−25%); the first frame was slower (12.1 vs 9.4 s). The saving is the fixed per-frame sync and BVH cost, so it shrinks as a share at final sample counts. # Highland cinematic film

A 29-second (plus end card), 2.39:1 owner film cut from the native Blender
walkthrough. It replaces the single continuous drone flight with nine composed
shots, a dusk exterior, an x-ray elevator section, graded picture, typography and
an original score. The doors, elevator rise and section are the same native
keyframes that `build_blender.py` validates; the edit only chooses where each
camera looks. The edit follows the archviz film skill
(`.claude/skills/archviz-film-upgrade/SKILL.md`).

| # | Shot | Film time | Native frames | Lens | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Arrival | 0.00–4.50 s | 1–108 | 24 mm, shifted | Dusk establishing view of the east frontage with title |
| 02 | Entry | 4.50–7.50 s | 66–137 | 28 mm | Push to the east glazing as the entry doors open |
| 03 | Lobby | 7.50–10.50 s | 150–221 | 24 mm | Lobby 110 toward the connector |
| 04 | Slats | 10.50–12.75 s | 222–275 | 50 mm f/2.8 | Insert along the walnut feature wall, focused at frame centre |
| 05 | Corridor 108 | 12.75–15.75 s | 200–271 | 24 mm | Slider past residence doors toward Elevator M1 |
| 06 | Elevator | 15.75–18.75 s | 280–351 | 26 mm | Symmetrical landing-door reveal |
| 07 | Section | 18.75–21.75 s | 378–449 | 35 mm | X-ray R1 to R2 rise with live datum readout |
| 08 | Corridor 208 | 21.75–24.75 s | 470–541 | 24 mm | Push toward Stair M1 |
| 09 | Release | 24.75–29.25 s | 1–108 | 24 mm, shifted | Back outside: slow pull-back from the entry to the lit dusk facade, fade to the end card |

Every camera is level and lens-shifted, so verticals stay vertical. The
exception is the section shot, which looks down at the cut building. Lenses stay
at 24–35 mm, except the 50 mm detail insert. Shot lengths are whole beats at
80 BPM, and the score's chord changes land on the cuts. The film no longer ends in
a corridor: shot 09 returns outside (compression and release). Native frames 1–146
are the only ones with the exterior shown, so shot 09 reuses the arrival's frames;
the entry doors begin to swing open from its frame 66, small in the wide view.
The skill asks for a sunlit release; this film is set at dusk, so the release is open
sky and the warmly lit facade, not sun. The street in front of the east facade is
only about 25 m wide (OSM massing across it starts at x = 2456 in), so the 24 mm
exterior cameras gain distance along the street, not across it: shot 01 arrives from
the south, shot 09 leaves to the north-east. `cinema.py --reuse` refuses to render a
prepared scene whose camera validation failed or is out of date.

Filler area, point and spot lights are hidden from camera and glossy rays
(`light_hygiene`), so they light surfaces without leaving hotspots on glass, doors
or wet paving; the fixtures still reflect through their emissive meshes. The scene
keeps persistent data between frames of one render process.

## Files

- `cinema.shots.json`: the edit. Camera keys use plan inches in the exterior study's
  coordinate system, plus lens, shift, aperture, focus point, label and exposure trim.
- `cinema.py`: opens the validated walkthrough scene and adds the following:
  - dusk sky, lit windows and wet pavement;
  - scanned materials and models (below), lever hardware and an elevator call station;
  - windows on the neighboring massing, calmer luminaires and the lobby slat wall;
  - the x-ray section treatment and one camera per shot.

  It saves `Highland-cinema.blend`, renders frames per shot (resumable) and validates
  camera clearance and smoothness at every film frame.
- `cinema_assets.py` and `assets/polyhaven-cinema.lock.json`: Poly Haven CC0 assets, locked
  by URL, size and MD5 and downloaded into `build/assets/polyhaven` (about 190 MB, not committed):
  - walnut veneer (doors, frames, slats, cab), plaster relief (walls, ceilings);
  - limestone tile (lobby and cab floors), brick (facade), wet asphalt and concrete pavers;
  - street trees, lobby plants, two lounge chairs and a side table, post-top street lamps, a hydrant.

  Textures are box-projected at their real-world size, so the procedural boxes need no UVs.
- `cinema_score.py`: original NumPy score and sound design. The chords follow the cuts.
  The door swing, landing chime, cab run and arrival ding come from native scene frames.
- `cinema_finish.py`: Lanczos upscale (when needed), halation, S-curve, split-tone,
  lens aberration, vignette, grain, scope letterbox, titles, chapter labels,
  section gauge and end card. It masters audio with two-pass `loudnorm` to −16 LUFS / −1.5 dBTP
  and encodes two-pass 10 Mbit/s H.264. It also writes stills, a shot sheet, a GIF and checks.

## Rebuild

Python 3.11 from the repo-wide uv lock. `bpy==5.0.1` needs NumPy 1.26, so the lock pins
`opencv-python-headless` 4.10 (later releases pull NumPy 2) and one environment covers the
scene, score and finish.

```bash
uv sync --group vision

uv run python projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema_assets.py           # CC0 assets, checksum-verified
uv run python projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema.py --validate --profile proof --step 12   # quick look
uv run python projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema.py --reuse --profile local                # all 702 frames
uv run python projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema_finish.py --profile local
```

| Profile | Render size | Max samples | Where | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proof` | 640 × 268 | 8 | CPU, ~8 s/frame | Framing checks |
| `local` | 1280 × 536 | 20 | 4-core CPU, ~35–60 s/frame (~8 h) | CPU fallback, upscaled 1.5× in finishing |
| `final` | 1920 × 804 | 128 | GPU (`--device OPTIX`) | Native 1080p master |
| `uhd` | 3840 × 1608 | 96 | GPU | 4K master (`cinema_finish.py --master 2160`) |

GPU rendering on RunPod, with a benchmark that projects the run time, is in [RUNPOD.md](RUNPOD.md).
`--worker k/n` splits frames across parallel processes; `--bench` times one frame per shot.

`cinema.py` builds and validates the base walkthrough itself when its report is missing,
failed or stale. `--shots`, `--step` and `--only` render subsets, and existing frames
are skipped, so an interrupted render resumes where it stopped. Each frame folder is
bound to the prepared scene and its settings (`SCENE.json`). After any change to the
scene code, assets or cameras, frames from the old scene are moved aside, not reused.

## What is illustrative

The floor datums (R1 353.00 / R2 363.25 ft) and the circulation rectangles come
from the sources listed in `README.md`. Everything else seen in this film is a
presentation treatment and must not be read as documented:

- the dusk lighting, wet pavement, street lights and lit windows;
- the walnut slat wall and all other finishes, furnishings, hardware and planting;
- the street trees, street lamps and hydrant, which keep the study's tree positions but not its species;
- the elevator car, its door timing and the x-ray section;
- the neighboring massing (OSM, with approximate heights).

The film carries a persistent on-screen note and a full end-card statement.

}

def emission(mat, strength, color=None):
    b = mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = strength
    if color:
        b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (*color, 1)


def dusk(scene):
    """Blue-hour exterior: deep sky, lit apartments, wet street reflections."""
    world = scene.world.node_tree
    n, l = world.nodes, world.links
    env = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'TEX_ENVIRONMENT')
    bg = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'BACKGROUND')
    tint = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); tint.data_type = 'RGBA'; tint.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'
    tint.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    tint.inputs['B'].default_value = (.28, .42, .95, 1)
    l.new(env.outputs['Color'], tint.inputs['A']); l.new(tint.outputs['Result'], bg.inputs['Color'])
    bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = .55
    for o in scene.objects:
        if o.type == 'LIGHT' and o.data.type == 'SUN':
            o.data.energy = .06; o.data.color = (.55, .65, 1)
    emission(bpy.data.materials['Apartment warm interior'], 1.5, (1, .5, .2))
    emission(bpy.data.materials['Apartment linen'], .4, (1, .7, .45))
    # Neighborhood massing gets a sparse grid of warm and cool windows so the
    # street reads as inhabited. Massing heights and windows remain illustrative.
    mat = bpy.data.materials['Neighborhood massing']
    n, l = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links
    b = n.get('Principled BSDF')
    coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
    sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(coord.outputs['Object'], sep.inputs[0])
    along = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); along.operation = 'ADD'
    l.new(sep.outputs['X'], along.inputs[0]); l.new(sep.outputs['Y'], along.inputs[1])
    grid = n.new('ShaderNodeCombineXYZ')
    for axis, src, pitch in (('X', along.outputs[0], 3.1), ('Y', sep.outputs['Z'], 3.3)):
        m = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = 'DIVIDE'; m.inputs[1].default_value = pitch
        l.new(src, m.inputs[0]); l.new(m.outputs[0], grid.inputs[axis])
    cells = n.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath'); cells.operation = 'FLOOR'; l.new(grid.outputs[0], cells.inputs[0])
    frac = n.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath'); frac.operation = 'FRACTION'; l.new(grid.outputs[0], frac.inputs[0])
    fs = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(frac.outputs[0], fs.inputs[0])
    mask = None
    for axis, lo, hi in (('X', .25, .75), ('Y', .3, .78)):
        a = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); a.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; a.inputs[1].default_value = lo; l.new(fs.outputs[axis], a.inputs[0])
        c = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); c.operation = 'LESS_THAN'; c.inputs[1].default_value = hi; l.new(fs.outputs[axis], c.inputs[0])
        both = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); both.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(a.outputs[0], both.inputs[0]); l.new(c.outputs[0], both.inputs[1])
        if mask:
            m = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(mask, m.inputs[0]); l.new(both.outputs[0], m.inputs[1]); mask = m.outputs[0]
        else:
            mask = both.outputs[0]
    rnd = n.new('ShaderNodeTexWhiteNoise'); rnd.noise_dimensions = '3D'; l.new(cells.outputs[0], rnd.inputs['Vector'])
    lit = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); lit.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; lit.inputs[1].default_value = .72; l.new(rnd.outputs['Value'], lit.inputs[0])
    on = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); on.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(lit.outputs[0], on.inputs[0]); l.new(mask, on.inputs[1])
    gain = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); gain.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; gain.inputs[1].default_value = .3; l.new(on.outputs[0], gain.inputs[0])
    hue = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); hue.data_type = 'RGBA'; hue.inputs['A'].default_value = (1, .55, .24, 1); hue.inputs['B'].default_value = (.75, .85, 1, 1)
    l.new(rnd.outputs['Color'], hue.inputs['Factor'])
    l.new(hue.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Emission Color']); l.new(gain.outputs[0], b.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    # Wet pavement: low roughness broken up by puddle noise.
    for name in ('road', 'paving', 'Damp pavement', 'ground', 'concrete'):
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat or mat.get('texture'):  # scanned surfaces carry their own puddles
            continue
        n, l = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links
        b = n.get('Principled BSDF')
        coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
        noise = n.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise'); noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = .35
        noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 4
        l.new(coord.outputs['Object'], noise.inputs['Vector'])
        ramp = n.new('ShaderNodeMapRange')
        ramp.inputs['From Min'].default_value = .46; ramp.inputs['From Max'].default_value = .56
        ramp.inputs['To Min'].default_value = .5 if name != 'road' else .32
        ramp.inputs['To Max'].default_value = .06
        l.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Value']); l.new(ramp.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Roughness'])
        dark = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); dark.data_type = 'RGBA'; dark.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'
        dark.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1; dark.inputs['B'].default_value = (.55, .58, .62, 1)
        src = b.inputs['Base Color'].links[0].from_socket if b.inputs['Base Color'].is_linked else None
        if src:
            l.new(src, dark.inputs['A'])
        else:
            dark.inputs['A'].default_value = b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value[:]
        l.new(dark.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Base Color'])


def exterior_only(obj):
    for f, v in [(1, False), (146, False), (147, True)]:
        obj.hide_render = v; obj.keyframe_insert('hide_render', frame=f)
    return obj


def street_lights(scene, col, lib):
    """Illustrative post-top lamps along the east sidewalk; not a site survey."""
    for name, strength in (('street_lamp_01_bulb', 40), ('street_lamp_01_glass', 2.5)):
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if mat:
            emission(mat, strength, (1, .72, .42))
    for y in (380, 980, 1720):
        x = 1790; z = A.ground(scene, x*I, y*I)
        exterior_only(A.instance(lib, 'street_lamp_01', col, (x*I, y*I, z), yaw=math.pi, name='Street lamp'))
        d = bpy.data.lights.new('Street light pool', 'POINT'); d.energy = 700; d.color = (1, .7, .4); d.shadow_soft_size = .15
        o = bpy.data.objects.new(d.name, d); col.objects.link(o); o.location = (x*I, y*I, z+3.45)
        exterior_only(o)


def dress(scene, data):
    """Scanned CC0 materials and models in place of the procedural stand-ins.
    Placement and finishes are illustrative presentation choices."""
    T = lambda name: bpy.data.materials[name]
    A.pbr(T('Satin walnut doors'), data, 'american_walnut_veneer', tint=(.36, .21, .12), rough=(.22, .42), bump=.12, vertical=True)
    A.pbr(T('Dark walnut frames'), data, 'american_walnut_veneer', tint=(.17, .1, .065), rough=(.25, .45), bump=.1, vertical=True)
    A.pbr(T('Gallery plaster'), data, 'white_plaster_02', tint=(.89, .85, .77), rough=(.6, .8), bump=.04, variation=.12)
    A.pbr(T('Warm plaster ceiling'), data, 'white_plaster_02', tint=(.97, .95, .9), rough=(.75, .9), bump=.02, variation=.08)
    for name in ('Honed lobby stone', 'Elevator solid stone floor'):
        A.pbr(T(name), data, 'marble_01', tint=(.92, .9, .86), rough=(.12, .3), bump=.08)
    for name in ('brick-x', 'brick-y'):
        A.pbr(T(name), data, 'brick_wall_001', tint=(.9, .82, .78), rough=(.72, .95), bump=.45)
    A.pbr(T('road'), data, 'clean_asphalt', tint=(.55, .57, .6), rough=(.5, .75), bump=.25, wet=True)
    A.pbr(T('Damp pavement'), data, 'clean_asphalt', tint=(.5, .52, .56), rough=(.5, .75), bump=.25, wet=True)
    A.pbr(T('paving'), data, 'concrete_pavement', tint=(.8, .8, .8), rough=(.55, .8), bump=.3, wet=True)
    lib = A.library(scene, data)
    col = bpy.data.collections.new('Cinema / illustrative dressing (Poly Haven CC0)'); scene.collection.children.link(col)
    # The photo-informed street trees keep their positions; scanned trees replace the
    # procedural trunks, branches and leaf clouds.
    trunks = [(o.name, o.matrix_world@Vector(o.bound_box[0]), o.matrix_world@Vector(o.bound_box[6]))
              for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith('tree-trunk-')]
    for o in list(scene.objects):
        if o.name.startswith('tree-') or o.name.startswith('Fine canopy twig') or '-crown-' in o.name:
            bpy.data.objects.remove(o, do_unlink=True)
    rng = random.Random(208)
    for name, lo, hi in trunks:
        x, y = (lo.x+hi.x)/2, (lo.y+hi.y)/2
        exterior_only(A.instance(lib, 'tree_small_02', col, (x, y, A.ground(scene, x, y)), yaw=rng.uniform(0, math.tau),
                                 scale=rng.uniform(.95, 1.12), name='Street tree / '+name))
    exterior_only(A.instance(lib, 'fire_hydrant', col, (1782*I, 1150*I, A.ground(scene, 1782*I, 1150*I)), yaw=math.pi/2, name='Hydrant'))
    street_lights(scene, col, lib)
    # Lobby: scanned planters replace the low-poly ones; a lounge pair faces the slat wall.
    for o in list(scene.objects):
        if o.name.startswith(('Indoor plant', 'Lobby stone planter')):
            bpy.data.objects.remove(o, do_unlink=True)
    floor = 132*I
    for x, y in ((1140, 1388), (1330, 1392)):
        A.instance(lib, 'potted_plant_01', col, (x*I, y*I, floor), yaw=rng.uniform(0, math.tau), name='Lobby plant')
    for x in (1196, 1272):
        A.instance(lib, 'mid_century_lounge_chair', col, (x*I, 1291*I, floor), yaw=math.pi, name='Lobby lounge chair')
    A.instance(lib, 'side_table_01', col, (1234*I, 1278*I, floor), name='Lobby side table')
    hardware(scene)
    scene['cinema_assets'] = 'Poly Haven CC0: '+', '.join(sorted(data['assets']))


def cylinder(name, radius, depth, loc, rot, mat, col, segments=24):
    import bmesh
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm = bmesh.new()
    bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, segments=segments, radius1=radius, radius2=radius, depth=depth)
    for f in bm.faces:
        f.smooth = True
    bm.to_mesh(mesh); bm.free(); mesh.materials.append(mat)
    o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh); col.objects.link(o); o.location = loc; o.rotation_euler = rot
    o['basis'] = 'Illustrative hardware; no hardware schedule reviewed'
    return o


def hardware(scene):
    """Lever handles on rosettes replace block pulls; an elevator call station at R1 and R2."""
    brass = bpy.data.materials['Brushed champagne brass'].node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    brass.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (.78, .56, .28, 1); brass.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1
    bronze = bpy.data.materials['Satin elevator bronze'].node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    bronze.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (.2, .15, .1, 1)
    col = bpy.data.collections['Native interior / Lobby 110 and Corridors 108–208']
    mat = bpy.data.materials['Brushed champagne brass']
    for o in list(scene.objects):
        if not o.name.endswith(' pull') or 'residence door' not in o.name:
            continue
        lo = o.matrix_world@Vector(o.bound_box[0]); hi = o.matrix_world@Vector(o.bound_box[6])
        east = lo.x/I > 915  # east-wall doors face west into the corridor
        face = (lo.x if east else hi.x); out = -1 if east else 1
        y, z = (lo.y+hi.y)/2, lo.z+3.5*I
        cylinder(o.name+' rosette', 1.05*I, .35*I, (face+out*.18*I, y, z), (0, math.pi/2, 0), mat, col)
        cylinder(o.name+' lever neck', .28*I, 1.6*I, (face+out*.9*I, y, z), (0, math.pi/2, 0), mat, col, 12)
        cylinder(o.name+' lever', .3*I, 4.8*I, (face+out*1.7*I, y+(2.2 if y/I < 1300 else -2.2)*I*(1 if east else -1), z), (math.pi/2, 0, 0), mat, col, 12)
        bpy.data.objects.remove(o, do_unlink=True)
    steel = bpy.data.materials['Entrance stainless steel']
    glow = bpy.data.materials.new('Call button halo'); glow.use_nodes = True
    emission(glow, 6, (1, .78, .5))
    for z in (132, 255):
        B.box(f'R{1 if z == 132 else 2} elevator call plate', (879, 879.4, 1481, 1485, z+36, z+48), steel, col)
        for dz in (40, 44):
            cylinder(f'R{1 if z == 132 else 2} call button', .45*I, .25*I, (879.5*I, 1483*I, (z+dz)*I), (0, math.pi/2, 0), glow, col, 20)


def interior(scene):
    """Calmer luminaires so ceilings read as fixtures, not blown-out holes."""
    emission(bpy.data.materials['Warm LED diffuser'], 3.2)
    for o in scene.objects:
        if 'floor guidance' in o.name:
            o.hide_render = True; o.hide_viewport = True
        if o.type == 'LIGHT' and 'recessed wall wash' in o.name:
            o.data.energy = 26
        if o.type == 'LIGHT' and 'ceiling wash' in o.name:
            o.data.energy = 34

        l.new(facing.outputs['Facing'], edge.inputs[0]); l.new(transparent.outputs[0], edge.inputs[1]); l.new(glow.outputs[0], edge.inputs[2])

    for o in hide:

def camera(scene, rig, shot):
    cam = bpy.data.objects.new('Cinema / '+shot['id'], bpy.data.cameras.new('Cinema lens / '+shot['id']))
    rig.objects.link(cam)
    d = cam.data
    d.lens = shot['lens']; d.sensor_fit = 'HORIZONTAL'; d.sensor_width = 36
    d.shift_y = shot.get('shift_y', 0); d.clip_start = .03; d.clip_end = 600
    if shot.get('fstop'):
        d.dof.use_dof = True; d.dof.aperture_fstop = shot['fstop']; d.dof.aperture_blades = 7; d.dof.aperture_ratio = 1
    a, b = shot.get('ease', [0, 0])
    n = shot['frames']
    focus = Vector(shot['focus'])*I
    prev_yaw = None
    for j in range(n):
        f = shot['src_start']+j
        u = profile(j/(n-1), a, b)
        pos = sample(shot['keys'], u, 'pos')*I
        look = sample(shot['keys'], u, 'look')*I
        # A barely perceptible stabilized-head drift, a few millimetres.
        t = f/24
        pos += Vector((math.sin(t*1.3+n)*.002, math.sin(t*.9+2*n)*.002, math.sin(t*1.7)*.0015))
        direction = look-pos
        yaw = math.atan2(direction.y, direction.x)
        # atan2 wraps at +-pi; a camera looking along -x flips between +pi and -pi with the drift, and
        # Euler interpolation then spins a full turn inside the motion-blur shutter. Keep yaw continuous.
        if prev_yaw is not None:
            yaw += 2*math.pi*round((prev_yaw-yaw)/(2*math.pi))
        prev_yaw = yaw
        pitch = math.atan2(direction.z, math.hypot(direction.x, direction.y)) if shot.get('pitch') else 0
        cam.location = pos
        cam.rotation_euler = (math.pi/2+pitch, 0, yaw-math.pi/2)
        cam.keyframe_insert('location', frame=f); cam.keyframe_insert('rotation_euler', frame=f)
        if d.dof.use_dof:
            d.dof.focus_distance = (focus-pos).length; d.dof.keyframe_insert('focus_distance', frame=f)
    return cam


def base_validated(base):
    """The base scene must have passed build_blender.py's own checks for the current flight spec.
    The builder saves the .blend before validating, so file existence alone proves nothing."""
    report = base.with_suffix('.validation.json')
    if not base.exists() or not report.exists():
        return False
    r = json.loads(report.read_text())
    return (r.get('look') == 'archviz' and not r.get('wall_collisions') and not r.get('door_collisions')
            and r.get('max_camera_path_error_m', 1) <= .08 and r.get('max_return_rotation_step_deg', 99) <= 10
            and abs(r.get('r1_to_r2_rise_in', 0)-123) <= .001
            and r.get('source_spec_sha256') == hashlib.sha256(B.SPEC_FILE.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
