def dusk(scene):
    """Blue-hour exterior: deep sky, lit apartments, wet street reflections."""
    world = scene.world.node_tree
    n, l = world.nodes, world.links
    env = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'TEX_ENVIRONMENT')
    bg = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'BACKGROUND')
    tint = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); tint.data_type = 'RGBA'; tint.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'
    tint.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    tint.inputs['B'].default_value = (.28, .42, .95, 1)
    l.new(env.outputs['Color'], tint.inputs['A']); l.new(tint.outputs['Result'], bg.inputs['Color'])
    bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = .55
    for o in scene.objects:
        if o.type == 'LIGHT' and o.data.type == 'SUN':
            o.data.energy = .06; o.data.color = (.55, .65, 1)
    emission(bpy.data.materials['Apartment warm interior'], 1.5, (1, .5, .2))
    emission(bpy.data.materials['Apartment linen'], .4, (1, .7, .45))
    # Neighborhood massing gets a sparse grid of warm and cool windows so the
    # street reads as inhabited. Massing heights and windows remain illustrative.
    mat = bpy.data.materials['Neighborhood massing']
    n, l = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links
    b = n.get('Principled BSDF')
    coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
    sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(coord.outputs['Object'], sep.inputs[0])
    along = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); along.operation = 'ADD'
    l.new(sep.outputs['X'], along.inputs[0]); l.new(sep.outputs['Y'], along.inputs[1])
    grid = n.new('ShaderNodeCombineXYZ')
    for axis, src, pitch in (('X', along.outputs[0], 3.1), ('Y', sep.outputs['Z'], 3.3)):
        m = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = 'DIVIDE'; m.inputs[1].default_value = pitch
        l.new(src, m.inputs[0]); l.new(m.outputs[0], grid.inputs[axis])
    cells = n.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath'); cells.operation = 'FLOOR'; l.new(grid.outputs[0], cells.inputs[0])
    frac = n.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath'); frac.operation = 'FRACTION'; l.new(grid.outputs[0], frac.inputs[0])
    fs = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(frac.outputs[0], fs.inputs[0])
    mask = None
    for axis, lo, hi in (('X', .25, .75), ('Y', .3, .78)):
        a = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); a.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; a.inputs[1].default_value = lo; l.new(fs.outputs[axis], a.inputs[0])
        c = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); c.operation = 'LESS_THAN'; c.inputs[1].default_value = hi; l.new(fs.outputs[axis], c.inputs[0])
        both = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); both.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(a.outputs[0], both.inputs[0]); l.new(c.outputs[0], both.inputs[1])
        if mask:
            m = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(mask, m.inputs[0]); l.new(both.outputs[0], m.inputs[1]); mask = m.outputs[0]
        else:
            mask = both.outputs[0]
    rnd = n.new('ShaderNodeTexWhiteNoise'); rnd.noise_dimensions = '3D'; l.new(cells.outputs[0], rnd.inputs['Vector'])
    lit = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); lit.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; lit.inputs[1].default_value = .72; l.new(rnd.outputs['Value'], lit.inputs[0])
    on = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); on.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; l.new(lit.outputs[0], on.inputs[0]); l.new(mask, on.inputs[1])
    gain = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); gain.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; gain.inputs[1].default_value = .3; l.new(on.outputs[0], gain.inputs[0])
    hue = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); hue.data_type = 'RGBA'; hue.inputs['A'].default_value = (1, .55, .24, 1); hue.inputs['B'].default_value = (.75, .85, 1, 1)
    l.new(rnd.outputs['Color'], hue.inputs['Factor'])
    l.new(hue.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Emission Color']); l.new(gain.outputs[0], b.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    # Wet pavement: low roughness broken up by puddle noise.
    for name in ('road', 'paving', 'Damp pavement', 'ground', 'concrete'):
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat or mat.get('texture'):  # scanned surfaces carry their own puddles
            continue
        n, l = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links
        b = n.get('Principled BSDF')
        coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
        noise = n.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise'); noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = .35
        noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 4
        l.new(coord.outputs['Object'], noise.inputs['Vector'])
        ramp = n.new('ShaderNodeMapRange')
        ramp.inputs['From Min'].default_value = .46; ramp.inputs['From Max'].default_value = .56
        ramp.inputs['To Min'].default_value = .5 if name != 'road' else .32
        ramp.inputs['To Max'].default_value = .06
        l.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Value']); l.new(ramp.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Roughness'])
        dark = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); dark.data_type = 'RGBA'; dark.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'
        dark.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1; dark.inputs['B'].default_value = (.55, .58, .62, 1)
        src = b.inputs['Base Color'].links[0].from_socket if b.inputs['Base Color'].is_linked else None
        if src:
            l.new(src, dark.inputs['A'])
        else:
            dark.inputs['A'].default_value = b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value[:]
        l.new(dark.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Base Color'])

    v = min(1., max(0., (t-a)/(b-a)))
    return v*v*(3-2*v)


def grade(img, exposure, rng, upscaled):
    """Display-referred finishing: halation, gentle S-curve, split tone, lens and grain."""
    img = img*(2**exposure)
    lum = img@np.array([.2126, .7152, .0722], np.float32)
    hi = np.clip((img-.74)/.26, 0, 1)
    small = cv2.resize(hi, (PW//4, PH//4), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    glow = cv2.resize(cv2.GaussianBlur(small, (0, 0), 7), (PW, PH), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
    img = img+glow*np.array([1., .58, .36], np.float32)*.12
    if upscaled:
        img = img+.35*(img-cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (0, 0), 1.1*K))
    img = np.clip(img, 0, 1)
    img = img+(img*img*(3-2*img)-img)*.16
    w_shadow = ((1-lum)**2)[..., None]; w_light = (lum**2)[..., None]
    img = img+w_shadow*np.array([-.010, .002, .014], np.float32)+w_light*np.array([.012, .004, -.010], np.float32)
    img = .010+img*(1-.010)
    # Very slight lateral chromatic aberration, strongest at the frame edge.
    for ch, s in ((0, 1.0007), (2, .9993)):
        m = np.float32([[s, 0, (1-s)*PW/2], [0, s, (1-s)*PH/2]])
        img[..., ch] = cv2.warpAffine(img[..., ch], m, (PW, PH), flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REFLECT)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:PH, 0:PW].astype(np.float32)
    r = np.sqrt(((xx-PW/2)/(PW/2))**2+((yy-PH/2)/(PW/2))**2)/np.sqrt(1+(PH/PW)**2)
    img = img*(1-.24*r**2.4)[..., None]
    grain = cv2.GaussianBlur(rng.standard_normal((PH, PW)).astype(np.float32), (0, 0), .65*K)*.022
    img = img+(grain*(.55+.45*(1-np.clip(lum, 0, 1))))[..., None]
    return np.clip(img, 0, 1)

def reverb(x, seconds=2.8, wet=.32):
    n = int(seconds*SR); t = np.arange(n)/SR

# Keep the photo-informed tree placement and branching, replace opaque blobs
    # with individually shaped, curved leaves and small branch tips.
    crowns=[o for o in list(scene.objects) if '-crown-' in o.name or o.name.startswith('south-hedge-')]
    leaf_count=0
    for old in crowns:
        bb=[old.matrix_world@Vector(v) for v in old.bound_box]
        lo=Vector(tuple(min(v[j] for v in bb) for j in range(3)))
        hi=Vector(tuple(max(v[j] for v in bb) for j in range(3)))
        center=(lo+hi)/2;dims=hi-lo;count=700 if '-crown-' in old.name else 230
        leaf_cloud(old.name+' / individual leaves',center,dims,count,True);leaf_count+=count
        if '-crown-' in old.name:
            for j in range(5):
                end=center+Vector((rng.uniform(-1,1)*dims.x*.35,rng.uniform(-1,1)*dims.y*.35,rng.uniform(-.5,.5)*dims.z*.5))
                exterior_time(tube('Fine canopy twig',[center-Vector((0,0,.55)),end],.009,bark))
        bpy.data.objects.remove(old,do_unlink=True)

    # Window recesses: actual back panels, softly folded curtains and warm glow.
    curtain=material('Apartment linen',(.52,.43,.30),.9,emission=.12)
    warm=material('Apartment warm interior',(.65,.36,.13),.8,emission=.55)
    windows=[o for o in scene.objects if o.type=='MESH' and '-glazing' in o.name and any(f'-R{j}-' in o.name for j in (2,3,4,5))]
    lit_windows=0
    for window in windows:

"""Cinematic edit of the native Highland walkthrough.

Builds on the validated scene from build_blender.py: the doors, elevator, rise
and section stay native keyframes. This module adds a dusk exterior, refined
interior exposure, a clean x-ray treatment for the section, and one level,
lens-shifted camera per shot from cinema.shots.json. Frames render per shot
and can be resumed. Run with Python 3.11 and bpy==5.0.1.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import random
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import build_blender as B  # noqa: E402
import cinema_assets as A  # noqa: E402

SPEC_FILE = HERE / 'cinema.shots.json'
SPEC = json.loads(SPEC_FILE.read_text())
I = .0254
BUILD = ROOT / 'build/highland-cinema'
PROFILES = {
    # Scope 2.39:1: width, height, max samples, adaptive noise threshold.
    # cinema_finish.py scales proof/local frames to the master picture size.
    'proof': (640, 268, 8, .02),
    'local': (1280, 536, 20, .02),
    'final': (1920, 804, 128, .01),
    'uhd': (3840, 1608, 96, .01),
}


CAMERA_FIELDS = ('id', 'src_start', 'frames', 'lens', 'shift_y', 'fstop', 'pitch', 'ease', 'keys', 'focus')




def configure_device(scene, backend):
    """Select CPU, CUDA or OptiX; never fall back silently."""
    scene.cycles.device = 'CPU'
    if backend == 'CPU':
        return []
    prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences
    prefs.compute_device_type = backend
    prefs.get_devices()
    used = []
    for d in prefs.devices:
        d.use = d.type == backend
        if d.use:
            used.append(d.name)
    if not used:
        raise SystemExit(f'No {backend} device found; refusing to fall back to CPU')
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'
    scene.cycles.denoising_use_gpu = True
    print('Cycles devices:', used, flush=True)
    return used


def settings(scene, profile_name, samples=None):
    w, h, max_samples, threshold = PROFILES[profile_name]
    scene.render.resolution_x = w; scene.render.resolution_y = h; scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100
    scene.cycles.samples = samples or max_samples; scene.cycles.adaptive_threshold = threshold
    scene.cycles.adaptive_min_samples = min(32, scene.cycles.samples)


def frame_marker(scene):
    return {'source': scene['cinema_source_sha256'], 'resolution': [scene.render.resolution_x, scene.render.resolution_y],
            'samples': scene.cycles.samples, 'adaptive_threshold': round(scene.cycles.adaptive_threshold, 4)}


def claim_frames(scene, folder):
    """Bind a frame folder to this prepared scene and its render settings. Frames from any other
    scene or settings are moved aside, never deleted, so resuming can't mix stale frames."""
    root = BUILD/'frames'/folder; marker = root/'SCENE.json'; want = frame_marker(scene)
    have = json.loads(marker.read_text()) if marker.exists() else None
    if root.exists() and have != want and any(root.rglob('[0-9]*.png')):
        stale = root.with_name(f'{folder}.stale-{time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")}')
        root.rename(stale)
        print(f'Moved frames from a different scene or settings to {stale}', flush=True)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker.write_text(json.dumps(want, indent=2)+'\n')


def check_claim(scene, folder):
    marker = BUILD/'frames'/folder/'SCENE.json'
    if not marker.exists() or json.loads(marker.read_text()) != frame_marker(scene):
        raise SystemExit(f'frames/{folder} is not bound to this scene and settings; run with --claim-frames first')


def render(scene, shots, profile_name, step=1, only=None, worker=(0, 1), folder=None):
    # One process claims the folder; parallel workers only verify the claim.
    (claim_frames if worker[1] == 1 else check_claim)(scene, folder or profile_name)
    log = []
    index = -1
    for shot in SPEC['shots']:
        if shots and shot['id'] not in shots:
            continue
        cam = bpy.data.objects['Cinema / '+shot['id']]; scene.camera = cam
        out = BUILD/'frames'/(folder or profile_name)/shot['id']; out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        local = only if only else range(1, shot['frames']+1, step)
        for j in local:
            if not 1 <= j <= shot['frames']:
                continue
            # Workers interleave frames so each sees every shot's cost.
            index += 1
            if index % worker[1] != worker[0]:
                continue
            path = out/f'{j:04d}.png'
            if path.exists():
                continue
            scene.frame_set(shot['src_start']+j-1)
            scene.render.filepath = str(path.with_suffix('.tmp.png'))
            start = time.monotonic(); bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
            path.with_suffix('.tmp.png').rename(path)
            log.append((shot['id'], j, round(time.monotonic()-start, 1)))
            print(f'SHOT {shot["id"]} {j}/{shot["frames"]} {log[-1][2]}s', flush=True)
    return log


def bench(scene, profile_name):
    """Render one mid-shot frame per shot and project the full film."""
    folder = 'bench-'+profile_name
    (BUILD/'frames'/folder/SPEC['shots'][0]['id']/'0001.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
    for shot in SPEC['shots']:
        f = BUILD/'frames'/folder/shot['id']/f'{shot["frames"]//2:04d}.png'
        f.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    # The first frame also pays kernel loading; render a warm-up first.
    render(scene, [SPEC['shots'][0]['id']], profile_name, only=[1], folder=folder)
    log = []
    for shot in SPEC['shots']:
        log += render(scene, [shot['id']], profile_name, only=[shot['frames']//2], folder=folder)
    per = {sid: t for sid, _, t in log}
    total = sum(per[s['id']]*s['frames'] for s in SPEC['shots'])
    report = {'profile': profile_name, 'resolution': PROFILES[profile_name][:2], 'samples': scene.cycles.samples,
              'device': scene.cycles.device, 'seconds_per_frame': per,
              'projected_hours_one_worker': round(total/3600, 2), 'frames': sum(s['frames'] for s in SPEC['shots'])}
    (BUILD/f'bench-{profile_name}.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+'\n')
    print('BENCH', json.dumps(report), flush=True)


def main():
    if '--' in sys.argv:  # blender -b -P cinema.py -- args
        sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]]+sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--')+1:]
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--base', type=Path, default=ROOT/'build/highland-blender/Highland-walkthrough.blend')
    p.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=BUILD/'Highland-cinema.blend')
    p.add_argument('--reuse', action='store_true', help='Open --output instead of preparing it again')
    p.add_argument('--profile', choices=PROFILES, default='proof')
    p.add_argument('--shots', default='', help='Comma-separated shot IDs; default all')
    p.add_argument('--step', type=int, default=1, help='Render every Nth frame (previews)')
    p.add_argument('--only', default='', help='Comma-separated shot-local frame numbers')
    p.add_argument('--threads', type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument('--validate', action='store_true', help='Check camera clearance and smoothness at every film frame')
    p.add_argument('--device', choices=['CPU', 'CUDA', 'OPTIX'], default='CPU')
    p.add_argument('--samples', type=int, help='Override the profile maximum samples')
    p.add_argument('--worker', default='0/1', help='k/n: render every nth frame starting at k, for parallel processes')
    p.add_argument('--bench', action='store_true', help='Time one frame per shot and project the film')
    p.add_argument('--claim-frames', action='store_true', help='Bind the profile frame folder to this scene before parallel workers start')
    a = p.parse_args()

"""Original score and sound design for the Highland cinematic film.

Everything is synthesized here with NumPy, so no licensed music or sample
library is involved. Chords change on the picture cuts and effects land on the
native door, chime and elevator events, all derived from cinema.shots.json.
"""
import json
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SPEC = json.loads((HERE/'cinema.shots.json').read_text())
FPS = SPEC['fps']
SR = 48_000
END_CARD = 3.0
TAIL = .75
RNG = np.random.default_rng(200)


def timeline():
    """Output cut times (s) and a map from native scene frames to film time."""
    cuts, t = [], 0.
    for shot in SPEC['shots']:
        cuts.append((shot['id'], t, shot))
        t += shot['frames']/FPS
    return cuts, t


def film_time(src_frame, shot_id):
    for sid, start, shot in timeline()[0]:
        if sid == shot_id and shot['src_start'] <= src_frame < shot['src_start']+shot['frames']:
            return start+(src_frame-shot['src_start'])/FPS
    raise ValueError(f'Frame {src_frame} is not in shot {shot_id}')


def midi(n):
    return 440*2**((n-69)/12)


def shape(x, lo=None, hi=None, order=2):
    """Zero-phase Butterworth-shaped filter applied in the frequency domain."""
    spec = np.fft.rfft(x, axis=0)

"""Film v2 look upgrades for the Highland cinematic film (bpy 5.0.1).

cinema.prepare() calls these after its own dusk/interior/x-ray passes, on the scene it has just built
from code. The saved Highland-cinema.blend is regenerated on every prepare, so nothing here edits a
hand-tuned file. Before a material is changed, its node tree is copied to a fake-user material named
'<name> / v1 backup' (see backup()), so the previous shader can be compared in the .blend.

Each upgrade has a CONFIG dict at the top of its section. Everything here is a presentation
treatment: lamp colours, window occupancy, blinds, bevels and section graphics are illustrative,
not documented conditions.

Brief-to-code notes (Blender 5.0.1, checked against this build):
- `scene.use_nodes`/`scene.node_tree`, `glare.glare_type` and `lens.use_projector` are 4.x APIs.
  The compositor here is `scene.compositing_node_group`; glare and lens settings are input sockets.
- Musgrave was merged into Noise in Blender 4.1; the micro-roughness uses Noise plus Voronoi.
- Fog glow, lens dispersion and film grain already run once, in cinema_finish.grade(), on the
  rendered frames. Running them again in the compositor would double them, so color() leaves them alone.
"""
import math

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

I = .0254
EXTERIOR_LAST = 146  # native frames 1-146 are the only ones that show the exterior (see cinema.exterior_only)


def srgb(hex_code):
    """'#E6B87A' -> linear RGB."""
    c = [int(hex_code.lstrip('#')[k:k+2], 16)/255 for k in (0, 2, 4)]
    return tuple(v/12.92 if v <= .04045 else ((v+.055)/1.055)**2.4 for v in c)


def backup(mat):
    """Copy the material once, before its first v2 change, as a fake-user '<name> / v1 backup'."""
    name = mat.name+' / v1 backup'
    if name not in bpy.data.materials:
        copy = mat.copy(); copy.name = name; copy.use_fake_user = True
    return mat


def bsdf(mat):
    return next((n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED'), None)


def source(sock):
    """Linked output feeding a socket, or None."""
    return sock.links[0].from_socket if sock.is_linked else None


def exterior_keys(obj):
    for f, v in [(1, False), (EXTERIOR_LAST, False), (EXTERIOR_LAST+1, True)]:
        obj.hide_render = v; obj.keyframe_insert('hide_render', frame=f)
    return obj


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 1: color management
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COLOR = {
    'view_transform': 'AgX',
    # Medium High Contrast was tried against the finish's own S-curve and crushed the corridor
    # shadows; Base Contrast plus the finish curve gives the same contrast with shadow detail.
    'look': 'AgX - Base Contrast',
    'exposure': 0.0,
    'gamma': 1.0,
}


def color(scene, cfg=COLOR):
    vs = scene.view_settings
    vs.view_transform = cfg['view_transform'] if cfg['view_transform'] in [
        i.identifier for i in vs.bl_rna.properties['view_transform'].enum_items] else 'Filmic'
    vs.look = cfg['look'] if vs.view_transform == 'AgX' else 'None'
    vs.exposure = cfg['exposure']; vs.gamma = cfg['gamma']


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 2: blue-hour world, street lamps and atmosphere
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BLUE_HOUR = {
    'hdri': None,                # optional path to a blue-hour HDRI; None keeps the scene's tinted sky HDRI
    'hdri_rotation_deg': 0.0,
    'sky_zenith': (.020, .040, .135),    # camera-visible sky, linear
    'sky_horizon': (.20, .17, .25),      # faint violet afterglow at the horizon
    'sky_cloud_mix': .55,                # how much the HDRI's clouds modulate the visible gradient
    'sky_camera_strength': 1.0,
    'lamp_kelvin': 2900,
    'lamp_point_w': 220,                 # small omni share for the lamp head and nearby facade
    'lamp_spot_w': 1100,                 # downward pool on the pavement
    'lamp_spot_deg': 118, 'lamp_spot_blend': .6, 'lamp_radius_m': .22,
    'volume_density': .0015, 'volume_anisotropy': .6,
    # Streetscape box in plan inches (exterior study coordinates): sidewalk, street and entry.
    'volume_box_in': (1480, 2440, -300, 2500, 60, 760),
}


def blue_hour(scene, cfg=BLUE_HOUR):
    world = scene.world; n, l = world.node_tree.nodes, world.node_tree.links
    env = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'TEX_ENVIRONMENT')
    bg = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'BACKGROUND')
    out = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'OUTPUT_WORLD')
    if cfg['hdri']:
        env.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(cfg['hdri']), check_existing=True)
    mapping = next((x for x in n if x.type == 'MAPPING'), None)
    if mapping:
        mapping.inputs['Rotation'].default_value[2] = math.radians(cfg['hdri_rotation_deg'])
    # Camera rays see a blue-hour gradient carrying the HDRI's clouds; every other ray keeps the
    # existing tinted HDRI as the light. The two are graded independently.
    coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord'); sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ')
    l.new(coord.outputs['Generated'], sep.inputs[0])
    ramp = n.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB'); l.new(sep.outputs['Z'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    ramp.color_ramp.interpolation = 'EASE'
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.; ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (*cfg['sky_horizon'], 1)
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = .55; ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (*cfg['sky_zenith'], 1)
    lum = n.new('ShaderNodeRGBToBW'); l.new(env.outputs['Color'], lum.inputs['Color'])
    cloud = n.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); l.new(lum.outputs['Val'], cloud.inputs['Value'])
    cloud.inputs['To Min'].default_value = 1-cfg['sky_cloud_mix']; cloud.inputs['To Max'].default_value = 1+cfg['sky_cloud_mix']
    sky = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); sky.data_type = 'RGBA'; sky.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'; sky.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    l.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], sky.inputs['A']); l.new(cloud.outputs['Result'], sky.inputs['B'])
    cam_bg = n.new('ShaderNodeBackground'); cam_bg.name = 'Blue hour / camera sky'
    l.new(sky.outputs['Result'], cam_bg.inputs['Color']); cam_bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['sky_camera_strength']
    bg.name = 'Blue hour / environment light'
    path = n.new('ShaderNodeLightPath'); mix = n.new('ShaderNodeMixShader')
    l.new(path.outputs['Is Camera Ray'], mix.inputs['Fac'])
    l.new(bg.outputs['Background'], mix.inputs[1]); l.new(cam_bg.outputs['Background'], mix.inputs[2])
    l.new(mix.outputs['Shader'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    # Street lamps: 2900 K blackbody bulbs, a soft omni share and a downward pool.
    for name in ('street_lamp_01_bulb', 'street_lamp_01_glass'):
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat:
            continue
        backup(mat); b = bsdf(mat)
        bb = mat.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBlackbody'); bb.inputs['Temperature'].default_value = cfg['lamp_kelvin']
        mat.node_tree.links.new(bb.outputs['Color'], b.inputs['Emission Color'])
    lamps = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'LIGHT' and o.name.startswith('Street light pool')]
    col = lamps[0].users_collection[0] if lamps else scene.collection
    for o in lamps:
        d = o.data; d.energy = cfg['lamp_point_w']; d.shadow_soft_size = cfg['lamp_radius_m']
        d.use_temperature = True; d.temperature = cfg['lamp_kelvin']; d.color = (1, 1, 1)
        s = bpy.data.lights.new('Street lamp downward pool', 'SPOT')
        s.energy = cfg['lamp_spot_w']; s.spot_size = math.radians(cfg['lamp_spot_deg']); s.spot_blend = cfg['lamp_spot_blend']
        s.shadow_soft_size = cfg['lamp_radius_m']; s.use_temperature = True; s.temperature = cfg['lamp_kelvin']
        so = bpy.data.objects.new(s.name, s); col.objects.link(so)
        so.location = o.location+Vector((0, 0, -.05)); so.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)  # spot points down -Z
        so.visible_camera = False; so.visible_glossy = False
        exterior_keys(so)

    # Thin homogeneous atmosphere over the streetscape, exterior frames only.
    x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 = cfg['volume_box_in']
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new('Streetscape atmosphere')
    vs = [(x*I, y*I, z*I) for z in (z0, z1) for x, y in ((x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1))]
    mesh.from_pydata(vs, [], [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)])
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new('Streetscape atmosphere'); nt = mat.node_tree
    nt.nodes.remove(bsdf(mat))
    vol = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.inputs['Density'].default_value = cfg['volume_density']; vol.inputs['Anisotropy'].default_value = cfg['volume_anisotropy']
    vol.inputs['Color'].default_value = (.85, .88, 1, 1)
    nt.links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], next(x for x in nt.nodes if x.type == 'OUTPUT_MATERIAL').inputs['Volume'])
    mesh.materials.append(mat)
    box = bpy.data.objects.new('Streetscape atmosphere (illustrative)', mesh); col.objects.link(box)
    box.visible_shadow = False
    exterior_keys(box)
    return box


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 3: lit apartment windows
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WINDOWS = {
    'recess_prefix': 'Warm apartment recess ',
    'curtain_name': 'Apartment curtain fold',
    'kelvin': (2500, 3800),
    # Occupancy tiers on the per-window seed: below 'off' dark, below 'bright' medium, else bright.
    'off': .28, 'bright': .80,
    'strength_off': .03, 'strength_medium': 1.3, 'strength_bright': 2.6,
    'blinds_share': .55,         # share of lit windows with blinds lowered
    'blinds_pitch_m': .035, 'blinds_transmission': .35,
    'glass_ior': 1.52, 'glass_roughness': .04,
    'curtain_glow': .35,         # linen glow relative to the window behind it
}


def windows(scene, cfg=WINDOWS):
    """Per-window seeds as an object attribute shared by a recess, its curtains and its glass, so
    one window reads as one room: same colour temperature, same occupancy, blinds at one height."""
    recesses = [o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['recess_prefix'])]
    if not recesses:
        return 0
    for j, o in enumerate(sorted(recesses, key=lambda o: o.name)):
        # Deterministic, well spread seeds (golden-ratio sequence) instead of Object Info > Random,
        # because the curtains are separate objects that must share their window's seed.
        o['window_seed'] = (j*.6180339887+.31) % 1
    centers = [(o, o.matrix_world@(sum((Vector(c) for c in o.bound_box), Vector())/8)) for o in recesses]
    for c in (o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['curtain_name'])):
        p = c.matrix_world@(sum((Vector(v) for v in c.bound_box), Vector())/8)
        c['window_seed'] = min(centers, key=lambda oc: (oc[1]-p).length)[0]['window_seed']
    for o in recesses:
        glass = bpy.data.objects.get(o.name[len(cfg['recess_prefix']):])
        if glass:
            glass['window_seed'] = o['window_seed']
            for m in glass.data.materials:
                b = bsdf(m)
                b.inputs['IOR'].default_value = cfg['glass_ior']; b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = cfg['glass_roughness']

    def seed_nodes(nt):
        n, l = nt.nodes, nt.links
        attr = n.new('ShaderNodeAttribute'); attr.attribute_type = 'OBJECT'; attr.attribute_name = 'window_seed'
        return attr.outputs['Fac']

    def math(nt, op, a, b=None, clamp=False):
        m = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = op; m.use_clamp = clamp
        for k, v in enumerate((a, b)):
            if v is None:
                continue
            if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
                m.inputs[k].default_value = v
            else:
                nt.links.new(v, m.inputs[k])
        return m.outputs[0]

    def strength(nt, seed):
        """Stepped occupancy: off / medium / bright."""
        lo = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', seed, cfg['off'])
        hi = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', seed, cfg['bright'])
        s = math(nt, 'ADD', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', lo, cfg['strength_medium']-cfg['strength_off']),
                 math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', hi, cfg['strength_bright']-cfg['strength_medium']))
        return math(nt, 'ADD', s, cfg['strength_off'])

    def kelvin(nt, seed):
        # Decorrelate colour from occupancy with a second hash of the seed.
        h = math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 7.31))
        k = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); nt.links.new(h, k.inputs['Value'])
        k.inputs['To Min'].default_value, k.inputs['To Max'].default_value = cfg['kelvin']
        bb = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBlackbody'); nt.links.new(k.outputs['Result'], bb.inputs['Temperature'])
        return bb.outputs['Color']

    # Recess back panel: colour, occupancy and lowered blinds.
    mat = backup(bpy.data.materials['Apartment warm interior']); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)
    seed = seed_nodes(nt)
    s = strength(nt, seed)
    coord = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord'); sep = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ')
    nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Object'], sep.inputs[0])
    wave = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexWave'); wave.wave_type = 'BANDS'; wave.bands_direction = 'Z'
    wave.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 1/cfg['blinds_pitch_m']/2
    nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Object'], wave.inputs['Vector'])
    slats = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); nt.links.new(wave.outputs['Fac'], slats.inputs['Value'])
    slats.inputs['To Min'].default_value = cfg['blinds_transmission']; slats.inputs['To Max'].default_value = 1
    # Blinds hang from the head of the window down to a per-window height. The recess boxes carry
    # world-space vertices, so the drop is measured against the object's own bounds.
    bounds = {}
    for o in (o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['recess_prefix'])):
        zs = [(o.matrix_world@Vector(v)).z for v in o.bound_box]
        o['window_z'] = (min(zs), max(zs))
        bounds[o.name] = o['window_z']
    zattr = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute'); zattr.attribute_type = 'OBJECT'; zattr.attribute_name = 'window_z'
    zv = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); nt.links.new(zattr.outputs['Vector'], zv.inputs[0])
    h2 = math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 3.97))
    drop = math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', h2, .85)                              # 0-85% of the window height
    height = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', zv.outputs['Y'], zv.outputs['X'])
    stop = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', zv.outputs['Y'], math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', height, drop))
    covered = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', sep.outputs['Z'], stop)
    has = math(nt, 'LESS_THAN', math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 5.23)), cfg['blinds_share'])
    blind = math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', covered, has)
    # emission factor = 1 where open, slat pattern where covered
    open_part = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', 1., blind)
    shade = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath'); shade.operation = 'MULTIPLY_ADD'
    nt.links.new(blind, shade.inputs[0]); nt.links.new(slats.outputs['Result'], shade.inputs[1]); nt.links.new(open_part, shade.inputs[2])
    nt.links.new(math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', s, shade.outputs[0]), b.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    nt.links.new(kelvin(nt, seed), b.inputs['Emission Color'])

    # Curtains glow with their own window: same colour, scaled occupancy.
    mat = backup(bpy.data.materials['Apartment linen']); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)
    seed = seed_nodes(nt)
    nt.links.new(math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', strength(nt, seed), cfg['curtain_glow']), b.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    tint = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMix'); tint.data_type = 'RGBA'; tint.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'; tint.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    tint.inputs['B'].default_value = (1, .85, .7, 1)
    nt.links.new(kelvin(nt, seed), tint.inputs['A']); nt.links.new(tint.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Emission Color'])
    return len(recesses)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 4: interior micro-bevels, micro-roughness and entry glazing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SURFACES = {
    # material: (bevel radius m or None, roughness variation +-)
    'Satin walnut doors': (.003, .06),          # residence doors, cab panels and the lobby slats
    'Dark walnut frames': (.003, .05),
    'Brushed champagne brass': (.0015, .04),
    'Satin elevator bronze': (.002, .04),
    'Gallery plaster': (.004, .06),             # wall corners and returns
    'Warm plaster ceiling': (None, .04),
    'Honed lobby stone': (None, .06),
    'Elevator solid stone floor': (None, .05),
    'Woven corridor carpet': (None, .04),
    'Charcoal ceramic planters': (.008, .05),
    'concrete': (.008, .06),                    # entry steps, edges and site concrete
    'mid_century_lounge_chair': (None, .05),    # leather chairs: scanned geometry, roughness only
    'Recessed entry mat': (None, .03),
}
BEVEL_SAMPLES = 4
ENTRY_GLASS = {'material': 'Entry glass', 'ior': 1.52, 'roughness': 0., 'tint': (.93, .97, .955),
               'edge_tint': (.55, .74, .70), 'edge_blend': .35}


def surfaces(scene, cfg=SURFACES):
    for name, (radius, amp) in cfg.items():
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat or not mat.node_tree:
            continue
        backup(mat); nt = mat.node_tree; n, l = nt.nodes, nt.links
        for b in [x for x in n if x.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED']:
            x, y = b.location
            if radius and not any(x.type == 'BEVEL' for x in n):
                bev = n.new('ShaderNodeBevel'); bev.samples = BEVEL_SAMPLES; bev.location = (x-260, y-420)
                bev.inputs['Radius'].default_value = radius
                old = source(b.inputs['Normal'])
                if old:  # chain the existing bump/normal map through the bevel
                    l.new(old, bev.inputs['Normal'])
                l.new(bev.outputs['Normal'], b.inputs['Normal'])
            if amp:
                coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
                noise = n.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise'); noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 2.5
                noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 6; noise.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = .55
                vor = n.new('ShaderNodeTexVoronoi'); vor.feature = 'SMOOTH_F1'; vor.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 18
                for t in (noise, vor):
                    l.new(coord.outputs['Object'], t.inputs['Vector'])
                blend = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); blend.data_type = 'FLOAT'; blend.inputs['Factor'].default_value = .35
                l.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], blend.inputs['A']); l.new(vor.outputs['Distance'], blend.inputs['B'])
                # Narrow band around the mean -> +-amp, so the scanned roughness map stays in charge.
                band = n.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); l.new(blend.outputs['Result'], band.inputs['Value'])
                band.inputs['From Min'].default_value = .3; band.inputs['From Max'].default_value = .7
                band.inputs['To Min'].default_value = -amp; band.inputs['To Max'].default_value = amp
                add = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); add.operation = 'ADD'; add.use_clamp = True
                old = source(b.inputs['Roughness'])
                if old:
                    l.new(old, add.inputs[0])
                else:
                    add.inputs[0].default_value = b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value
                l.new(band.outputs['Result'], add.inputs[1]); l.new(add.outputs[0], b.inputs['Roughness'])
    # Entry glazing: clear low-iron-ish glass, green-blue at grazing angles where the path through
    # the edge is longest. Reflections come from the Principled Fresnel at IOR 1.52.
    g = ENTRY_GLASS; mat = bpy.data.materials.get(g['material'])
    if mat:
        backup(mat); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)
        b.inputs['IOR'].default_value = g['ior']; b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = g['roughness']
        lw = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeLayerWeight'); lw.inputs['Blend'].default_value = g['edge_blend']
        mix = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMix'); mix.data_type = 'RGBA'
        mix.inputs['A'].default_value = (*g['tint'], 1); mix.inputs['B'].default_value = (*g['edge_tint'], 1)
        nt.links.new(lw.outputs['Facing'], mix.inputs['Factor']); nt.links.new(mix.outputs['Result'], b.inputs['Base Color'])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 5: two-tier x-ray section graphics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION = {
    'primary_keywords': ('floor', 'ceiling', 'slab', 'shaft', 'roof'),
    'primary_color': '#E6B87A', 'primary_strength': 2.5, 'primary_wire_m': .0045, 'shaft_wire_m': .007,
    'secondary_color': '#A67C52', 'secondary_strength': 1.6, 'secondary_opacity': .35, 'secondary_wire_m': .0018,
    # Translucent fill on horizontal faces of the ghosted floors/ceilings so R1 and R2 read as volumes.
    'fill_materials': {'Woven corridor carpet': .13, 'Honed lobby stone': .13, 'Warm plaster ceiling': .08},
    'fill_color': '#E6B87A', 'fill_strength': .35,
}


def section(scene, cfg=SECTION):
    primary = backup(bpy.data.materials['Section brass edges'])
    b = bsdf(primary)
    b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['primary_color']), 1)
    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = cfg['primary_strength']
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['primary_color']), 1)
    secondary = bpy.data.materials.new('Section bronze partition lines'); nt = secondary.node_tree
    nt.nodes.remove(bsdf(secondary))
    em = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['secondary_color']), 1); em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['secondary_strength']
    tr = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent'); mix = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMixShader')
    mix.inputs['Fac'].default_value = cfg['secondary_opacity']
    nt.links.new(tr.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1]); nt.links.new(em.outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
    nt.links.new(mix.outputs[0], next(x for x in nt.nodes if x.type == 'OUTPUT_MATERIAL').inputs['Surface'])
    counts = {'primary': 0, 'secondary': 0}
    for o in scene.objects:
        is_shaft = o.name == 'Elevator shaft / section reference'
        if not (o.name.endswith(' / section edges') or is_shaft):
            continue
        tier = 'primary' if is_shaft or any(k in o.name.lower() for k in cfg['primary_keywords']) else 'secondary'
        counts[tier] += 1
        if tier == 'secondary':
            o.data.materials.clear(); o.data.materials.append(secondary)
        for m in o.modifiers:
            if m.type == 'WIREFRAME':
                m.thickness = cfg['shaft_wire_m'] if is_shaft else cfg[tier+'_wire_m']
    for name, alpha in cfg['fill_materials'].items():
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat:
            continue
        nt = mat.node_tree; n, l = nt.nodes, nt.links
        wrap = n.get('Elevator architectural section')
        xray = source(wrap.inputs[2])
        geo = n.new('ShaderNodeNewGeometry'); sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(geo.outputs['Normal'], sep.inputs[0])
        up = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); up.operation = 'ABSOLUTE'; l.new(sep.outputs['Z'], up.inputs[0])
        flat = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); flat.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; flat.inputs[1].default_value = .7; l.new(up.outputs[0], flat.inputs[0])
        fac = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); fac.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; fac.inputs[1].default_value = alpha; l.new(flat.outputs[0], fac.inputs[0])
        em = n.new('ShaderNodeEmission'); em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['fill_color']), 1)
        em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['fill_strength']
        fill = n.new('ShaderNodeMixShader'); l.new(fac.outputs[0], fill.inputs['Fac'])
        l.new(xray, fill.inputs[1]); l.new(em.outputs[0], fill.inputs[2]); l.new(fill.outputs[0], wrap.inputs[2])
    return counts


def apply(scene):
    color(scene)
    blue_hour(scene)
    lit = windows(scene)
    surfaces(scene)
    tiers = section(scene)
    scene['cinema_v2'] = f'look v2: blue-hour world split, 2900 K lamps + atmosphere, {lit} varied windows, bevels, ' \
                         f'micro-roughness, entry glass, section tiers {tiers}'
    print('LOOK v2', scene['cinema_v2'], flush=True)

toolu_014Zrsmy2T19Ya2GYUjXcBrc.content:
"""Film v2 look upgrades for the Highland cinematic film (bpy 5.0.1).

cinema.prepare() calls these after its own dusk/interior/x-ray passes, on the scene it has just built
from code. The saved Highland-cinema.blend is regenerated on every prepare, so nothing here edits a
hand-tuned file. Before a material is changed, its node tree is copied to a fake-user material named
'<name> / v1 backup' (see backup()), so the previous shader can be compared in the .blend.

Each upgrade has a CONFIG dict at the top of its section. Everything here is a presentation
treatment: lamp colours, window occupancy, blinds, bevels and section graphics are illustrative,
not documented conditions.

Brief-to-code notes (Blender 5.0.1, checked against this build):
- `scene.use_nodes`/`scene.node_tree`, `glare.glare_type` and `lens.use_projector` are 4.x APIs.
  The compositor here is `scene.compositing_node_group`; glare and lens settings are input sockets.
- Musgrave was merged into Noise in Blender 4.1; the micro-roughness uses Noise plus Voronoi.
- Fog glow, lens dispersion and film grain already run once, in cinema_finish.grade(), on the
  rendered frames. Running them again in the compositor would double them, so color() leaves them alone.
"""
import math

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

I = .0254
EXTERIOR_LAST = 146  # native frames 1-146 are the only ones that show the exterior (see cinema.exterior_only)


def srgb(hex_code):
    """'#E6B87A' -> linear RGB."""
    c = [int(hex_code.lstrip('#')[k:k+2], 16)/255 for k in (0, 2, 4)]
    return tuple(v/12.92 if v <= .04045 else ((v+.055)/1.055)**2.4 for v in c)


def backup(mat):
    """Copy the material once, before its first v2 change, as a fake-user '<name> / v1 backup'."""
    name = mat.name+' / v1 backup'
    if name not in bpy.data.materials:
        copy = mat.copy(); copy.name = name; copy.use_fake_user = True
    return mat


def bsdf(mat):
    return next((n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED'), None)


def source(sock):
    """Linked output feeding a socket, or None."""
    return sock.links[0].from_socket if sock.is_linked else None


def exterior_keys(obj):
    for f, v in [(1, False), (EXTERIOR_LAST, False), (EXTERIOR_LAST+1, True)]:
        obj.hide_render = v; obj.keyframe_insert('hide_render', frame=f)
    return obj


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 1: color management
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COLOR = {
    'view_transform': 'AgX',
    # Medium High Contrast was tried against the finish's own S-curve and crushed the corridor
    # shadows; Base Contrast plus the finish curve gives the same contrast with shadow detail.
    'look': 'AgX - Base Contrast',
    'exposure': 0.0,
    'gamma': 1.0,
}


def color(scene, cfg=COLOR):
    vs = scene.view_settings
    vs.view_transform = cfg['view_transform'] if cfg['view_transform'] in [
        i.identifier for i in vs.bl_rna.properties['view_transform'].enum_items] else 'Filmic'
    vs.look = cfg['look'] if vs.view_transform == 'AgX' else 'None'
    vs.exposure = cfg['exposure']; vs.gamma = cfg['gamma']


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 2: blue-hour world, street lamps and atmosphere
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BLUE_HOUR = {
    'hdri': None,                # optional path to a blue-hour HDRI; None keeps the scene's tinted sky HDRI
    'hdri_rotation_deg': 0.0,
    'sky_zenith': (.020, .040, .135),    # camera-visible sky, linear
    'sky_horizon': (.20, .17, .25),      # faint violet afterglow at the horizon
    'sky_cloud_mix': .55,                # how much the HDRI's clouds modulate the visible gradient
    'sky_camera_strength': 1.0,
    'lamp_kelvin': 2900,
    'lamp_point_w': 220,                 # small omni share for the lamp head and nearby facade
    'lamp_spot_w': 1100,                 # downward pool on the pavement
    'lamp_spot_deg': 118, 'lamp_spot_blend': .6, 'lamp_radius_m': .22,
    'volume_density': .0015, 'volume_anisotropy': .6,
    # Streetscape box in plan inches (exterior study coordinates): sidewalk, street and entry.
    'volume_box_in': (1480, 2440, -300, 2500, 60, 760),
}


def blue_hour(scene, cfg=BLUE_HOUR):
    world = scene.world; n, l = world.node_tree.nodes, world.node_tree.links
    env = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'TEX_ENVIRONMENT')
    bg = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'BACKGROUND')
    out = next(x for x in n if x.type == 'OUTPUT_WORLD')
    if cfg['hdri']:
        env.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(cfg['hdri']), check_existing=True)
    mapping = next((x for x in n if x.type == 'MAPPING'), None)
    if mapping:
        mapping.inputs['Rotation'].default_value[2] = math.radians(cfg['hdri_rotation_deg'])
    # Camera rays see a blue-hour gradient carrying the HDRI's clouds; every other ray keeps the
    # existing tinted HDRI as the light. The two are graded independently.
    coord = n.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord'); sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ')
    l.new(coord.outputs['Generated'], sep.inputs[0])
    ramp = n.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB'); l.new(sep.outputs['Z'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    ramp.color_ramp.interpolation = 'EASE'
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.; ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (*cfg['sky_horizon'], 1)
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = .55; ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (*cfg['sky_zenith'], 1)
    lum = n.new('ShaderNodeRGBToBW'); l.new(env.outputs['Color'], lum.inputs['Color'])
    cloud = n.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); l.new(lum.outputs['Val'], cloud.inputs['Value'])
    cloud.inputs['To Min'].default_value = 1-cfg['sky_cloud_mix']; cloud.inputs['To Max'].default_value = 1+cfg['sky_cloud_mix']
    sky = n.new('ShaderNodeMix'); sky.data_type = 'RGBA'; sky.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'; sky.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    l.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], sky.inputs['A']); l.new(cloud.outputs['Result'], sky.inputs['B'])
    cam_bg = n.new('ShaderNodeBackground'); cam_bg.name = 'Blue hour / camera sky'
    l.new(sky.outputs['Result'], cam_bg.inputs['Color']); cam_bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['sky_camera_strength']
    bg.name = 'Blue hour / environment light'
    path = n.new('ShaderNodeLightPath'); mix = n.new('ShaderNodeMixShader')
    l.new(path.outputs['Is Camera Ray'], mix.inputs['Fac'])
    l.new(bg.outputs['Background'], mix.inputs[1]); l.new(cam_bg.outputs['Background'], mix.inputs[2])
    l.new(mix.outputs['Shader'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    # Street lamps: 2900 K blackbody bulbs, a soft omni share and a downward pool.
    for name in ('street_lamp_01_bulb', 'street_lamp_01_glass'):
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat:
            continue
        backup(mat); b = bsdf(mat)
        bb = mat.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBlackbody'); bb.inputs['Temperature'].default_value = cfg['lamp_kelvin']
        mat.node_tree.links.new(bb.outputs['Color'], b.inputs['Emission Color'])
    lamps = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'LIGHT' and o.name.startswith('Street light pool')]
    col = lamps[0].users_collection[0] if lamps else scene.collection
    for o in lamps:
        d = o.data; d.energy = cfg['lamp_point_w']; d.shadow_soft_size = cfg['lamp_radius_m']
        d.use_temperature = True; d.temperature = cfg['lamp_kelvin']; d.color = (1, 1, 1)
        s = bpy.data.lights.new('Street lamp downward pool', 'SPOT')
        s.energy = cfg['lamp_spot_w']; s.spot_size = math.radians(cfg['lamp_spot_deg']); s.spot_blend = cfg['lamp_spot_blend']
        s.shadow_soft_size = cfg['lamp_radius_m']; s.use_temperature = True; s.temperature = cfg['lamp_kelvin']
        so = bpy.data.objects.new(s.name, s); col.objects.link(so)
        so.location = o.location+Vector((0, 0, -.05)); so.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)  # spot points down -Z
        so.visible_camera = False; so.visible_glossy = False
        exterior_keys(so)

    # Thin homogeneous atmosphere over the streetscape, exterior frames only.
    x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 = cfg['volume_box_in']
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new('Streetscape atmosphere')
    vs = [(x*I, y*I, z*I) for z in (z0, z1) for x, y in ((x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1))]
    mesh.from_pydata(vs, [], [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)])
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new('Streetscape atmosphere'); nt = mat.node_tree
    nt.nodes.remove(bsdf(mat))
    vol = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.inputs['Density'].default_value = cfg['volume_density']; vol.inputs['Anisotropy'].default_value = cfg['volume_anisotropy']
    vol.inputs['Color'].default_value = (.85, .88, 1, 1)
    nt.links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], next(x for x in nt.nodes if x.type == 'OUTPUT_MATERIAL').inputs['Volume'])
    mesh.materials.append(mat)
    box = bpy.data.objects.new('Streetscape atmosphere (illustrative)', mesh); col.objects.link(box)
    box.visible_shadow = False
    exterior_keys(box)
    return box


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 3: lit apartment windows
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WINDOWS = {
    'recess_prefix': 'Warm apartment recess ',
    'curtain_name': 'Apartment curtain fold',
    'kelvin': (2500, 3800),
    # Occupancy tiers on the per-window seed: below 'off' dark, below 'bright' medium, else bright.
    'off': .28, 'bright': .80,
    'strength_off': .03, 'strength_medium': 1.3, 'strength_bright': 2.6,
    'blinds_share': .55,         # share of lit windows with blinds lowered
    'blinds_pitch_m': .035, 'blinds_transmission': .35,
    'glass_ior': 1.52, 'glass_roughness': .04,
    'curtain_glow': .35,         # linen glow relative to the window behind it
}


def windows(scene, cfg=WINDOWS):
    """Per-window seeds as an object attribute shared by a recess, its curtains and its glass, so
    one window reads as one room: same colour temperature, same occupancy, blinds at one height."""
    recesses = [o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['recess_prefix'])]
    if not recesses:
        return 0
    for j, o in enumerate(sorted(recesses, key=lambda o: o.name)):
        # Deterministic, well spread seeds (golden-ratio sequence) instead of Object Info > Random,
        # because the curtains are separate objects that must share their window's seed.
        o['window_seed'] = (j*.6180339887+.31) % 1
    centers = [(o, o.matrix_world@(sum((Vector(c) for c in o.bound_box), Vector())/8)) for o in recesses]
    for c in (o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['curtain_name'])):
        p = c.matrix_world@(sum((Vector(v) for v in c.bound_box), Vector())/8)
        c['window_seed'] = min(centers, key=lambda oc: (oc[1]-p).length)[0]['window_seed']
    for o in recesses:
        glass = bpy.data.objects.get(o.name[len(cfg['recess_prefix']):])
        if glass:
            glass['window_seed'] = o['window_seed']
            for m in glass.data.materials:
                b = bsdf(m)
                b.inputs['IOR'].default_value = cfg['glass_ior']; b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = cfg['glass_roughness']

    def seed_nodes(nt):
        n, l = nt.nodes, nt.links
        attr = n.new('ShaderNodeAttribute'); attr.attribute_type = 'OBJECT'; attr.attribute_name = 'window_seed'
        return attr.outputs['Fac']

    def math(nt, op, a, b=None, clamp=False):
        m = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath'); m.operation = op; m.use_clamp = clamp
        for k, v in enumerate((a, b)):
            if v is None:
                continue
            if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
                m.inputs[k].default_value = v
            else:
                nt.links.new(v, m.inputs[k])
        return m.outputs[0]

    def strength(nt, seed):
        """Stepped occupancy: off / medium / bright."""
        lo = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', seed, cfg['off'])
        hi = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', seed, cfg['bright'])
        s = math(nt, 'ADD', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', lo, cfg['strength_medium']-cfg['strength_off']),
                 math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', hi, cfg['strength_bright']-cfg['strength_medium']))
        return math(nt, 'ADD', s, cfg['strength_off'])

    def kelvin(nt, seed):
        # Decorrelate colour from occupancy with a second hash of the seed.
        h = math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 7.31))
        k = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); nt.links.new(h, k.inputs['Value'])
        k.inputs['To Min'].default_value, k.inputs['To Max'].default_value = cfg['kelvin']
        bb = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBlackbody'); nt.links.new(k.outputs['Result'], bb.inputs['Temperature'])
        return bb.outputs['Color']

    # Recess back panel: colour, occupancy and lowered blinds.
    mat = backup(bpy.data.materials['Apartment warm interior']); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)
    seed = seed_nodes(nt)
    s = strength(nt, seed)
    coord = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord'); sep = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ')
    nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Object'], sep.inputs[0])
    wave = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexWave'); wave.wave_type = 'BANDS'; wave.bands_direction = 'Z'
    wave.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 1/cfg['blinds_pitch_m']/2
    nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Object'], wave.inputs['Vector'])
    slats = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange'); nt.links.new(wave.outputs['Fac'], slats.inputs['Value'])
    slats.inputs['To Min'].default_value = cfg['blinds_transmission']; slats.inputs['To Max'].default_value = 1
    # Blinds hang from the head of the window down to a per-window height. The recess boxes carry
    # world-space vertices, so the drop is measured against the object's own bounds.
    bounds = {}
    for o in (o for o in scene.objects if o.name.startswith(cfg['recess_prefix'])):
        zs = [(o.matrix_world@Vector(v)).z for v in o.bound_box]
        o['window_z'] = (min(zs), max(zs))
        bounds[o.name] = o['window_z']
    zattr = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute'); zattr.attribute_type = 'OBJECT'; zattr.attribute_name = 'window_z'
    zv = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); nt.links.new(zattr.outputs['Vector'], zv.inputs[0])
    h2 = math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 3.97))
    drop = math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', h2, .85)                              # 0-85% of the window height
    height = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', zv.outputs['Y'], zv.outputs['X'])
    stop = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', zv.outputs['Y'], math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', height, drop))
    covered = math(nt, 'GREATER_THAN', sep.outputs['Z'], stop)
    has = math(nt, 'LESS_THAN', math(nt, 'FRACT', math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', seed, 5.23)), cfg['blinds_share'])
    blind = math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', covered, has)
    # emission factor = 1 where open, slat pattern where covered
    open_part = math(nt, 'SUBTRACT', 1., blind)
    shade = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath'); shade.operation = 'MULTIPLY_ADD'
    nt.links.new(blind, shade.inputs[0]); nt.links.new(slats.outputs['Result'], shade.inputs[1]); nt.links.new(open_part, shade.inputs[2])
    nt.links.new(math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', s, shade.outputs[0]), b.inputs['Emission Strength'])
    nt.links.new(kelvin(nt, seed), b.inputs['Emission Color'])

    mat = backup(bpy.data.materials['Apartment linen']); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)

    tint = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMix'); tint.data_type = 'RGBA'; tint.blend_type = 'MULTIPLY'; tint.inputs['Factor'].default_value = 1
    tint.inputs['B'].default_value = (1, .85, .7, 1)

    return len(recesses)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Task 4: interior micro-bevels, micro-roughness and entry glazing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SURFACES = {
    # material: (bevel radius m or None, roughness variation +-)
    'Satin walnut doors': (.003, .06),          # residence doors, cab panels and the lobby slats
    'Dark walnut frames': (.003, .05),
    'Brushed champagne brass': (.0015, .04),
    'Satin elevator bronze': (.002, .04),
    'Gallery plaster': (.004, .06),             # wall corners and returns
    'Warm plaster ceiling': (None, .04),
    'Honed lobby stone': (None, .06),
    'Elevator solid stone floor': (None, .05),
    'Woven corridor carpet': (None, .04),
    'Charcoal ceramic planters': (.008, .05),
    'concrete': (.008, .06),                    # entry steps, edges and site concrete
    'mid_century_lounge_chair': (None, .05),    # leather chairs: scanned geometry, roughness only
    'Recessed entry mat': (None, .03),

BEVEL_SAMPLES = 4
ENTRY_GLASS = {'material': 'Entry glass', 'ior': 1.52, 'roughness': 0., 'tint': (.93, .97, .955),
               'edge_tint': (.55, .74, .70), 'edge_blend': .35}


def surfaces(scene, cfg=SURFACES):

                band.inputs['From Min'].default_value = .3; band.inputs['From Max'].default_value = .7

    # Entry glazing: clear low-iron-ish glass, green-blue at grazing angles where the path through
    # the edge is longest. Reflections come from the Principled Fresnel at IOR 1.52.
    g = ENTRY_GLASS; mat = bpy.data.materials.get(g['material'])
    if mat:
        backup(mat); nt = mat.node_tree; b = bsdf(mat)
        b.inputs['IOR'].default_value = g['ior']; b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = g['roughness']
        lw = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeLayerWeight'); lw.inputs['Blend'].default_value = g['edge_blend']
        mix = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMix'); mix.data_type = 'RGBA'
        mix.inputs['A'].default_value = (*g['tint'], 1); mix.inputs['B'].default_value = (*g['edge_tint'], 1)

# Task 5: two-tier x-ray section graphics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION = {
    'primary_keywords': ('floor', 'ceiling', 'slab', 'shaft', 'roof'),
    'primary_color': '#E6B87A', 'primary_strength': 2.5, 'primary_wire_m': .0045, 'shaft_wire_m': .007,
    'secondary_color': '#A67C52', 'secondary_strength': 1.6, 'secondary_opacity': .35, 'secondary_wire_m': .0018,
    # Translucent fill on horizontal faces of the ghosted floors/ceilings so R1 and R2 read as volumes.
    'fill_materials': {'Woven corridor carpet': .13, 'Honed lobby stone': .13, 'Warm plaster ceiling': .08},
    'fill_color': '#E6B87A', 'fill_strength': .35,
}


def section(scene, cfg=SECTION):
    primary = backup(bpy.data.materials['Section brass edges'])
    b = bsdf(primary)
    b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['primary_color']), 1)
    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = cfg['primary_strength']
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['primary_color']), 1)
    secondary = bpy.data.materials.new('Section bronze partition lines'); nt = secondary.node_tree
    nt.nodes.remove(bsdf(secondary))
    em = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['secondary_color']), 1); em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['secondary_strength']
    tr = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent'); mix = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMixShader')
    mix.inputs['Fac'].default_value = cfg['secondary_opacity']
    nt.links.new(tr.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1]); nt.links.new(em.outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
    nt.links.new(mix.outputs[0], next(x for x in nt.nodes if x.type == 'OUTPUT_MATERIAL').inputs['Surface'])
    counts = {'primary': 0, 'secondary': 0}
    for o in scene.objects:
        is_shaft = o.name == 'Elevator shaft / section reference'
        if not (o.name.endswith(' / section edges') or is_shaft):
            continue
        tier = 'primary' if is_shaft or any(k in o.name.lower() for k in cfg['primary_keywords']) else 'secondary'

        for m in o.modifiers:
            if m.type == 'WIREFRAME':

    for name, alpha in cfg['fill_materials'].items():
        mat = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
        if not mat:

        nt = mat.node_tree; n, l = nt.nodes, nt.links
        wrap = n.get('Elevator architectural section')
        xray = source(wrap.inputs[2])
        geo = n.new('ShaderNodeNewGeometry'); sep = n.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ'); l.new(geo.outputs['Normal'], sep.inputs[0])
        up = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); up.operation = 'ABSOLUTE'; l.new(sep.outputs['Z'], up.inputs[0])
        flat = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); flat.operation = 'GREATER_THAN'; flat.inputs[1].default_value = .7; l.new(up.outputs[0], flat.inputs[0])
        fac = n.new('ShaderNodeMath'); fac.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; fac.inputs[1].default_value = alpha; l.new(flat.outputs[0], fac.inputs[0])
        em = n.new('ShaderNodeEmission'); em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (*srgb(cfg['fill_color']), 1)
        em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = cfg['fill_strength']
        fill = n.new('ShaderNodeMixShader'); l.new(fac.outputs[0], fill.inputs['Fac'])
        l.new(xray, fill.inputs[1]); l.new(em.outputs[0], fill.inputs[2]); l.new(fill.outputs[0], wrap.inputs[2])

    color(scene)
    blue_hour(scene)
    lit = windows(scene)
    surfaces(scene)
    tiers = section(scene)
    scene['cinema_v2'] = f'look v2: blue-hour world split, 2900 K lamps + atmosphere, {lit} varied windows, bevels, ' \
                         f'micro-roughness, entry glass, section tiers {tiers}'
